1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Maia_Sandu_at_Batumi_International_Conference%2C_on_19_July_2021_%28cropped%29.jpg/576px-Maia_Sandu_at_Batumi_International_Conference%2C_on_19_July_2021_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="688" data-file-height="1039" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center"><a href="/wiki/Maia_Sandu" title="Maia Sandu">Maia Sandu</a><br /><small><a href="/wiki/President_of_Moldova" title="President of Moldova">President</a><br />Since 2020</small></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>The 1994 <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Moldova_(1994)" title="Constitution of Moldova (1994)">Constitution of Moldova</a> sets the framework for the government of the country. A parliamentary majority of at least two-thirds is required to amend the <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Moldova" title="Constitution of Moldova">Constitution of Moldova</a>, which cannot be revised in times of war or national emergency. Amendments to the Constitution affecting the state's sovereignty, independence, or unity can only be made after a majority of voters support the proposal in a referendum. Furthermore, no revision can be made to limit the fundamental rights of people enumerated in the Constitution.<sup id="cite_ref-const2_163-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-const2-163">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup> The 1994 constitution also establishes an <a href="/wiki/Judicial_independence" title="Judicial independence">independent</a> <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Moldova" title="Constitutional Court of Moldova">Constitutional Court</a>, composed of six judges (two appointed by the President, two by Parliament, and two by the Supreme Council of <a href="/wiki/Magistrate" title="Magistrate">Magistrature</a>), serving six-year terms, during which they are irremovable and not subordinate to any power. The court is invested with the power of <a href="/wiki/Judicial_review" title="Judicial review">judicial review</a> over all <a href="/wiki/Act_of_Parliament" title="Act of Parliament">acts of parliament</a>, over <a href="/wiki/Presidential_decree" class="mw-redirect" title="Presidential decree">presidential decrees</a>, and over <a href="/wiki/Treaty" title="Treaty">international treaties</a> signed by the country.<sup id="cite_ref-const2_163-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-const2-163">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The head of state is the President of Moldova, who between 2001 and 2015 was elected by the Moldovan Parliament, requiring the support of three-fifths of the deputies (at least 61 votes). This system was designed to decrease executive authority in favour of the legislature. Nevertheless, the <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Moldova" title="Constitutional Court of Moldova">Constitutional Court</a> ruled on 4 March 2016 that this constitutional change adopted in 2000 regarding the presidential election was unconstitutional, thus reverting the election method of the president to a <a href="/wiki/Two-round_system" title="Two-round system">two-round system</a> <a href="/wiki/Direct_election" title="Direct election">direct election</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_relations">Foreign relations</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Moldova" title="Foreign relations of Moldova">Foreign relations of Moldova</a> and <a href="/wiki/Moldova%E2%80%93European_Union_relations" title="Moldova–European Union relations">Moldova–European Union relations</a></div>
<p>After achieving independence from the Soviet Union, Moldova's foreign policy was designed with a view to establishing relations with other European countries, neutrality, and European Union integration. In May 1995 the country signed the <a href="/wiki/CIS_Interparliamentary_Assembly" title="CIS Interparliamentary Assembly">CIS Interparliamentary Assembly</a> Convention to become a member and was also admitted in July 1995 to the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a>.
</p><p>Moldova became a member state of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> the <a href="/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe" title="Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe">Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe</a> (OSCE), the <a href="/wiki/North_Atlantic_Cooperation_Council" class="mw-redirect" title="North Atlantic Cooperation Council">North Atlantic Cooperation Council</a>, the <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>, the <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">International Monetary Fund</a> and the <a href="/wiki/European_Bank_for_Reconstruction_and_Development" title="European Bank for Reconstruction and Development">European Bank for Reconstruction and Development</a> in 1992. 1994 saw Moldova became a participant in <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Partnership_for_Peace" title="Partnership for Peace">Partnership for Peace</a> programme. The <a href="/wiki/Organisation_internationale_de_la_Francophonie" title="Organisation internationale de la Francophonie">Francophonie</a> was joined in 1996 with the country joining the <a href="/wiki/World_Trade_Organization" title="World Trade Organization">World Trade Organization</a> in 2001 and the <a href="/wiki/International_Criminal_Court" title="International Criminal Court">International Criminal Court</a> in 2002.
</p><p>In 2005, Moldova and the European Union established an action plan that sought to improve cooperation between Moldova and the union. At the end of 2005, the <a href="/wiki/European_Union_Border_Assistance_Mission_to_Moldova_and_Ukraine" title="European Union Border Assistance Mission to Moldova and Ukraine">European Union Border Assistance Mission to Moldova and Ukraine</a> (EUBAM) was established at the joint request of the presidents of Moldova and Ukraine. EUBAM assists the Moldovan and Ukrainian governments in approximating their border and customs procedures to EU standards and offers support in both countries' fight against cross-border crime.
</p><p>After the 1990–1992 <a href="/wiki/War_of_Transnistria" class="mw-redirect" title="War of Transnistria">War of Transnistria</a>, Moldova sought a peaceful resolution to the conflict in the Transnistria region by working with Romania, Ukraine, and Russia, calling for international mediation, and co-operating with the OSCE and UN fact-finding and observer missions. The <a href="/wiki/Foreign_minister_of_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="Foreign minister of Moldova">foreign minister of Moldova</a>, <a href="/wiki/Andrei_Stratan" title="Andrei Stratan">Andrei Stratan</a>, repeatedly stated that the Russian troops stationed in the breakaway region were there against the will of the Moldovan government and called on them to leave "completely and unconditionally".<sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup> In 2012, a <a href="/wiki/2012_Moldova_security_zone_incident" title="2012 Moldova security zone incident">security zone incident</a> resulted in the death of a civilian, raising tensions with Russia.<sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Batumi_International_Conference,_on_19_July_2021_05_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Batumi_International_Conference%2C_on_19_July_2021_05_%28cropped%29.jpg/220px-Batumi_International_Conference%2C_on_19_July_2021_05_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Batumi_International_Conference%2C_on_19_July_2021_05_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-Batumi_International_Conference%2C_on_19_July_2021_05_%28cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Batumi_International_Conference%2C_on_19_July_2021_05_%28cropped%29.jpg/440px-Batumi_International_Conference%2C_on_19_July_2021_05_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2548" data-file-height="1699" /></a><figcaption>President of Georgia <a href="/wiki/Salome_Zourabichvili" title="Salome Zourabichvili">Salome Zourabichvili</a>, President of Moldova <a href="/wiki/Maia_Sandu" title="Maia Sandu">Maia Sandu</a>, President of Ukraine <a href="/wiki/Volodymyr_Zelenskyy" title="Volodymyr Zelenskyy">Volodymyr Zelenskyy</a> and <a href="/wiki/President_of_the_European_Council" title="President of the European Council">President of the European Council</a> <a href="/wiki/Charles_Michel" title="Charles Michel">Charles Michel</a> during the 2021 <a href="/wiki/Batumi" title="Batumi">Batumi</a> International Conference. In 2014, the EU signed <a href="/wiki/European_Union_Association_Agreement" title="European Union Association Agreement">Association Agreements</a> with the three states.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In September 2010, the <a href="/wiki/European_Parliament" title="European Parliament">European Parliament</a> approved a grant of €90 million to Moldova.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup> The money was to supplement US$570 million in International Monetary Fund loans,<sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup> World Bank and other bilateral support already granted to Moldova. In April 2010, Romania offered Moldova development aid worth of €100 million while the number of scholarships for Moldovan students doubled to 5,000.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup> According to a lending agreement signed in February 2010, Poland provided US$15 million as a component of its support for Moldova in its European integration efforts.<sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup> The first joint meeting of the Governments of Romania and Moldova, held in March 2012, concluded with several bilateral agreements in various fields.<sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup> The European orientation "has been the policy of Moldova in recent years and this is the policy that must continue," <a href="/wiki/Nicolae_Timofti" title="Nicolae Timofti">Nicolae Timofti</a> told lawmakers before <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_presidential_election,_2011%E2%80%932012" class="mw-redirect" title="Moldovan presidential election, 2011–2012">his election in 2012</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources#What_information_to_include" title="Wikipedia:Citing sources"><span title="A complete citation is needed. (December 2022)">full citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>On 29 November 2013, at a summit in <a href="/wiki/Vilnius" title="Vilnius">Vilnius</a>, Moldova signed an <a href="/wiki/European_Union_Association_Agreement" title="European Union Association Agreement">association agreement</a> with the European Union dedicated to the European Union's '<a href="/wiki/Eastern_Partnership" title="Eastern Partnership">Eastern Partnership</a>' with ex-Soviet countries.<sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup> The ex-Romanian President <a href="/wiki/Traian_B%C4%83sescu" title="Traian Băsescu">Traian Băsescu</a> stated that Romania will make all efforts for Moldova to join the EU as soon as possible. Likewise, Traian Băsescu declared that the <a href="/wiki/Unification_of_Moldova_with_Romania" class="mw-redirect" title="Unification of Moldova with Romania">unification of Moldova with Romania</a> is the next national project for Romania, as more than 75% of the population speaks Romanian.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Russia">Russia</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Moldova%E2%80%93Russia_relations" title="Moldova–Russia relations">Moldova–Russia relations</a></div>
<p>A document written in 2021 by the Russia's FSB's Directorate for Cross-Border Cooperation, titled "Strategic objectives of the Russian Federation in the Republic of Moldova" sets out a 10 year plan to destabilise Moldova. Using energy blackmail, political and elite sources in Moldova that are favourable to Russia and the Orthodox Church. Russia denies any such plan.<sup id="cite_ref-cnn163_176-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnn163-176">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>Religious leaders play a role in shaping foreign policy. Since the fall of the Soviet Union, the Russian Government has frequently used its connections with the <a href="/wiki/Russian_Orthodox_Church" title="Russian Orthodox Church">Russian Orthodox Church</a> to block and stymie the integration of former Soviet states like Moldova into the West.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In February 2023 Russia cancelled a 2012 decree underpinning Moldova's sovereignty.<sup id="cite_ref-cnn163_176-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnn163-176">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup> In May 2023 the government announced its intentions to withdraw from the Commonwealth of Independent States and the immediate suspension of its participation.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179">&#91;174&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup> In July 2023 Moldova passed a law on denunciation of the agreement on Moldova's membership in the <a href="/wiki/CIS_Interparliamentary_Assembly" title="CIS Interparliamentary Assembly">CIS Interparliamentary Assembly</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 25 July 2023, the Moldovan government summoned the Russian ambassador to Moldova, Oleg Vasnetsov, after media reports of alleged spying devices on the rooftop of their embassy in Chişinău.<sup id="cite_ref-:08_182-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:08-182">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup> On 26 July 2023, the Moldovan government expelled 45 Russian diplomats and embassy staff due to "hostile actions" intended to destabilise the Republic of Moldova, according to Foreign Minister Nicu Popescu.<sup id="cite_ref-:13_184-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:13-184">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup> On 30 July, the Russian embassy announced that it would suspend consular appointments "for technical reasons".<sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>The Moldovan <a href="/wiki/Security_and_Intelligence_Service_of_Moldova" title="Security and Intelligence Service of Moldova">Security and Intelligence Service</a> (SIS) also ended all partnership agreements with Russia's <a href="/wiki/Federal_Security_Service" title="Federal Security Service">FSB</a> after sending official notifications to the authorities in <a href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="European_Union_Accession">European Union Accession</span></h4>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Moldova_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Moldova to the European Union">Accession of Moldova to the European Union</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:European_Union_Moldova_Locator.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/European_Union_Moldova_Locator.svg/220px-European_Union_Moldova_Locator.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="225" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/European_Union_Moldova_Locator.svg/330px-European_Union_Moldova_Locator.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/European_Union_Moldova_Locator.svg/440px-European_Union_Moldova_Locator.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="593" data-file-height="606" /></a><figcaption>In June 2022, Moldova became a recognised candidate for membership of the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Moldova has set 2030 as the target date for EU Accession.<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Moldova signed the Association Agreement with the European Union in <a href="/wiki/Brussels" title="Brussels">Brussels</a> on 27 June 2014. The signing came after the accord was drafted in Vilnius in November 2013.<sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Moldova signed the membership application to join the EU on 3 March 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-190" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-190">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> On 23 June 2022, Moldova was officially granted <a href="/wiki/Potential_enlargement_of_the_European_Union" title="Potential enlargement of the European Union">candidate status</a> by EU leaders.<sup id="cite_ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup> The United Nations Development Programme is also providing assistance to Moldova in implementing the necessary reforms for full accession by 2030.<sup id="cite_ref-192" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-192">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup> The European Union's <a href="/wiki/High_Representative_of_the_Union_for_Foreign_Affairs_and_Security_Policy" title="High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy">High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy</a> <a href="/wiki/Josep_Borrell" title="Josep Borrell">Josep Borrell</a> has confirmed that the pathway to accession does not depend upon a resolution of the <a href="/wiki/Transnistria_conflict" title="Transnistria conflict">Transnistria conflict</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 27 June, Moldova signed a comprehensive free trade agreement with the <a href="/wiki/European_Free_Trade_Association" title="European Free Trade Association">European Free Trade Association</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-194" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-194">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup> On 28 June 2023, the European Union announced a €1.6 billion support and investment programme for Moldova, as well as confirming reductions in the price of mobile data and voice roaming charges in Moldova by European and Moldovan telecoms operators, as well as Moldova joining the EU's joint gas purchase platform.<sup id="cite_ref-195" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-195">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Security">Security</span></h3>
<p>The European Union created a <a href="/wiki/European_Union_Partnership_Mission_in_Moldova" title="European Union Partnership Mission in Moldova">Partnership Mission in Moldova</a> through its <a href="/wiki/Common_Security_and_Defence_Policy" title="Common Security and Defence Policy">Common Security and Defence Policy</a> on 24 April 2023. The mission seeks to support the government of Moldova in countering hybrid threats the country faces as a result of the <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-196" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-196">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>A memorandum dated 29 March 2023 stated that the mission aims at "enhancing the resilience of Moldova's security sector in the area of crisis management as well as enhancing resilience to hybrid threats, including cybersecurity, and countering foreign information manipulation and interference".<sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup> The initial mandate of the mission is expected to be for two years and it will be made up of up to 40 police and customs officers and judicial officials.<sup id="cite_ref-198" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-198">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-thebriefing.eu_199-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-thebriefing.eu-199">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-200" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-200">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Estonia" title="Estonia">Estonia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Latvia" title="Latvia">Latvia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lithuania" title="Lithuania">Lithuania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Germany" title="Germany">Germany</a>, <a href="/wiki/Poland" title="Poland">Poland</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sweden" title="Sweden">Sweden</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Czech_Republic" title="Czech Republic">Czech Republic</a>, <a href="/wiki/Portugal" title="Portugal">Portugal</a>, <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Denmark" title="Denmark">Denmark</a> have all voiced support for the mission.<sup id="cite_ref-thebriefing.eu_199-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-thebriefing.eu-199">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 2 February 2023 Moldova passed a law introducing criminal penalties for <a href="/wiki/Separatism" title="Separatism">separatism</a>, including prison terms. The law continues with penalties for financing and inciting separatism, plotting against Moldova, and collecting and stealing information that could harm the country's sovereignty, independence and integrity.<sup id="cite_ref-201" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-201">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Military_of_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="Military of Moldova">Military of Moldova</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Moldovan_army_Capt._Deli_Ianec,_left,_role-playing_as_an_Afghan_National_Army_officer,_and_U.S._Army_Capt._Trey_Marsh,_with_Iron_Troop,_3rd_Squadron,_2nd_Cavalry_Regiment,_review_pictures_taken_after_a_search_130311-A-PU716-004.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Moldovan_army_Capt._Deli_Ianec%2C_left%2C_role-playing_as_an_Afghan_National_Army_officer%2C_and_U.S._Army_Capt._Trey_Marsh%2C_with_Iron_Troop%2C_3rd_Squadron%2C_2nd_Cavalry_Regiment%2C_review_pictures_taken_after_a_search_130311-A-PU716-004.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Moldovan_army_Capt._Deli_Ianec%2C_left%2C_role-playing_as_an_Afghan_National_Army_officer%2C_and_U.S._Army_Capt._Trey_Marsh%2C_with_Iron_Troop%2C_3rd_Squadron%2C_2nd_Cavalry_Regiment%2C_review_pictures_taken_after_a_search_130311-A-PU716-004.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/Moldovan_army_Capt._Deli_Ianec%2C_left%2C_role-playing_as_an_Afghan_National_Army_officer%2C_and_U.S._Army_Capt._Trey_Marsh%2C_with_Iron_Troop%2C_3rd_Squadron%2C_2nd_Cavalry_Regiment%2C_review_pictures_taken_after_a_search_130311-A-PU716-004.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5616" data-file-height="3744" /></a><figcaption>A soldier of the <a href="/wiki/Military_of_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="Military of Moldova">Moldovan Army</a> at the Joint Multinational Readiness Center in <a href="/wiki/Hohenfels,_Bavaria" title="Hohenfels, Bavaria">Hohenfels</a>, Germany</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Moldovan armed forces consists of the <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_Ground_Forces" title="Moldovan Ground Forces">Ground Forces</a> and <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_Air_Force" title="Moldovan Air Force">Air Force</a>.
Moldova maintains a standing army of just 6,500 soldiers, and spends just 0.4 percent of its GDP on defence, far behind its regional neighbours.<sup id="cite_ref-:05_202-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:05-202">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Moldova accepted all relevant arms control obligations of the former Soviet Union. On 30 October 1992, Moldova ratified the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_on_Conventional_Armed_Forces_in_Europe" title="Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe">Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe</a>, which establishes comprehensive limits on key categories of conventional military equipment and provides for the destruction of weapons in excess of those limits. The country acceded to the provisions of the nuclear <a href="/wiki/Non-Proliferation_Treaty" class="mw-redirect" title="Non-Proliferation Treaty">Non-Proliferation Treaty</a> in October 1994 in <a href="/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C.">Washington, D.C.</a> It does not have nuclear, biological, chemical or radiological weapons. Moldova joined the <a href="/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization" class="mw-redirect" title="North Atlantic Treaty Organization">North Atlantic Treaty Organization</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Partnership_for_Peace" title="Partnership for Peace">Partnership for Peace</a> on 16 March 1994.
</p><p>Moldova is committed to a number of international and regional control of arms regulations such as the <a href="/wiki/Protocol_Against_the_Illicit_Manufacturing_of_and_Trafficking_in_Firearms" title="Protocol Against the Illicit Manufacturing of and Trafficking in Firearms">UN Firearms Protocol</a>, <a href="/wiki/Stability_Pact_for_Southeastern_Europe" title="Stability Pact for Southeastern Europe">Stability Pact Regional Implementation Plan</a>, the UN Programme of Action (PoA), and the <a href="/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe" title="Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe">OSCE</a> Documents on Stockpiles of Conventional Ammunition.<sup id="cite_ref-203" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-203">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup> Since declaring independence in 1991, Moldova has participated in UN peacekeeping missions in <a href="/wiki/Liberia" title="Liberia">Liberia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ivory_Coast" title="Ivory Coast">Côte d'Ivoire</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sudan" title="Sudan">Sudan</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Georgia_(country)" title="Georgia (country)">Georgia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-204" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-204">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-205" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-205">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup> On 12 November 2014, the US donated to Moldovan Armed Forces 39 <a href="/wiki/Humvees" class="mw-redirect" title="Humvees">Humvees</a> and 10 trailers, with a value of US$700,000, to the 22nd Peacekeeping Battalion of the Moldovan National Army to "increase the capability of Moldovan peacekeeping contingents."<sup id="cite_ref-206" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-206">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Moldova signed a military agreement with Romania to strengthen regional security in 2015. The agreement is part of Moldova's strategy to reform its military and cooperate with its neighbours.<sup id="cite_ref-207" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-207">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Since 2022, the army has begun a process of modernization, and has been provided with more than €87 million in support for the modernization of the defence sector and the strengthening of security through the <a href="/wiki/European_Peace_Facility" class="mw-redirect" title="European Peace Facility">European Peace Facility</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:05_202-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:05-202">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-208" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-208">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup> In October 2022, Defense Minister Anatolie Nosatii claimed that 90 percent of the country's military equipment is outdated and of Soviet origin, dating back to the 1960s and 1980s.<sup id="cite_ref-209" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-209">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup> In April 2023, Valeriu Mija, Secretary of State for Defence Policy and National Army Reform in the Defence Ministry, claimed that Moldova needed $275 million to modernize its armed forces, especially in light of <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russia's invasion of Ukraine</a> and the presence of <a href="/wiki/Russian_military_presence_in_Transnistria" title="Russian military presence in Transnistria">1,500 Russian soldiers in Transnistria</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-210" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-210">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup> In June 2023, Poland also sent a transport of military equipment worth €8 million (including <a href="/wiki/Unmanned_combat_aerial_vehicle" title="Unmanned combat aerial vehicle">drones</a>, laptops, <a href="/wiki/Explosive_ordnance_disposal" class="mw-redirect" title="Explosive ordnance disposal">explosive ordnance disposal equipment</a>, and ultrasound equipment) to the <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_Police" title="Moldovan Police">Moldovan police</a> to increase the country's internal security.<sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-212" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-212">&#91;207&#93;</a></sup> Analysts at the Center for European Policy Analysis have called for further western weapon donations.<sup id="cite_ref-213" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-213">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Human_rights">Human rights</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_Moldova" title="Human rights in Moldova">Human rights in Moldova</a></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Freedom_House" title="Freedom House">Freedom House</a> ranked Moldova as a "partly free" country with a score of 62/100 in 2023. They summarized their finds as follows: "Moldova has a competitive electoral environment, and <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_assembly" title="Freedom of assembly">freedoms of assembly</a>, <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_speech" title="Freedom of speech">speech</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_religion" title="Freedom of religion">religion</a> are mostly protected. Nonetheless, <a href="/wiki/Corruption_in_Moldova" title="Corruption in Moldova">pervasive corruption</a>, links between major political figures and powerful economic interests, and critical deficiencies in the justice sector and the rule of law all continue to hamper democratic governance."<sup id="cite_ref-214" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-214">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup> According to <a href="/wiki/Transparency_International" title="Transparency International">Transparency International</a>, Moldova's <a href="/wiki/Corruption_Perceptions_Index" title="Corruption Perceptions Index">Corruption Perceptions Index</a> improved to 39 points in 2022 from 34 in 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-215" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-215">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Reporters_Without_Borders" title="Reporters Without Borders">Reporters Without Borders</a> improved Moldova's <a href="/wiki/World_Press_Freedom_Index" title="World Press Freedom Index">Press Freedom Index</a> ranking from 89th in 2020 to 40th in 2022, while cautioning that "Moldova's media are diverse but extremely polarised, like the country itself, which is marked by political instability and excessive influence by oligarchs."<sup id="cite_ref-216" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-216">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-217" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-217">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to <a href="/wiki/Amnesty_International" title="Amnesty International">Amnesty International</a>'s 2022/23 report, "No visible progress was made in reducing instances of torture and other ill-treatment in detention. Impunity continued for past human rights violations by law enforcement agencies. New "temporary" restrictions on public assemblies were introduced. The rights of <a href="/wiki/Intersex_and_LGBT" title="Intersex and LGBT">LGBTI</a> people were not fully realized, leading to cases of harassment, discrimination and violence. Some refugee reception centres turned away religious and ethnic minority refugees. In the breakaway Transdniestria region, prosecution and imprisonment for peaceful dissent continued."<sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup> On 18 June 2023, some 500 LGBT activists and supporters held a <a href="/wiki/Pride_parade" title="Pride parade">Pride parade</a> in the capital city of Chișinău which for the first time needed no heavy police cordons to protect them from protesters largely linked to the Orthodox church.<sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219">&#91;214&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to <a href="/wiki/United_States%27_Country_Reports_on_Human_Rights_Practices" class="mw-redirect" title="United States&#39; Country Reports on Human Rights Practices">Human Rights Report</a> of the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State" title="United States Department of State">United States Department of State</a>, released in 2022, "While authorities investigated reports of human rights abuses and corruption committed by officials, the process was slow and burdensome. During the year, authorities indicted and detained several former high-level officials including former President Igor Dodon, former member of parliament Vladimir Andronachi, Shor Party member of parliament Marina Tauber and former director of Moldovan Railways Anatolie Topala. None of these cases resulted in conviction by a court at year's end. Authorities took some steps to identify, investigate, and prosecute officials for human rights abuses, but progress was slow."<sup id="cite_ref-:5_220-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-220">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In a meeting with the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> in October 2022, EU representatives "welcomed positive developments in Moldova such as the ratification of the <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Convention" title="Istanbul Convention">Istanbul Convention</a> on preventing and combating violence against women, the adoption of legislation on <a href="/wiki/Hate_crime" title="Hate crime">hate crime</a>, and the ongoing work to reform the Electoral Code. It encouraged Moldovan authorities to address shortcomings identified by OSCE/ODIHR and the <a href="/wiki/Venice_Commission" title="Venice Commission">Venice Commission</a> across all areas and ensure effective and continuous implementation of human rights legislation."<sup id="cite_ref-221" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-221">&#91;216&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Office_for_Democratic_Institutions_and_Human_Rights" title="Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights">Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights</a>' 2016 recommendations on hate crimes were "largely reflected in amendments to the Criminal Code adopted by the Moldovan Parliament and published on 3 June 2022", but the report notes that Moldovan law enforcement officers often fail to record the bias motivations behind hate crimes, and additionally recommended "developing its victim support system to ensure effective access to justice, assistance, and protection services for hate crime victims".<sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222">&#91;217&#93;</a></sup> In 2021, 8 hate crimes were recorded, 7 of which reached a succcessful conviction, with one going to prosecution but without a conviction.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Administrative_divisions">Administrative divisions</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Moldova" title="Administrative divisions of Moldova">Administrative divisions of Moldova</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="List of cities in Moldova">List of cities in Moldova</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_localities_in_Moldova" title="List of localities in Moldova">List of localities in Moldova</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Communes_of_Moldova" title="Communes of Moldova">Communes of Moldova</a></div>

<div style="position:absolute; font-size:85%; left:57px; top:216px"><i><a href="/wiki/Rom%C3%A2nia" class="mw-redirect" title="România"><span style="color: grey;">Romania</span></a></i></div>
<div style="position:absolute; font-size:85%; left:274px; top:132px"><i><a href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine"><span style="color: grey;">Ukraine</span></a></i></div>
</div>
<p>Moldova is divided into 32 districts (<i>raioane</i>, singular <i><a href="/wiki/Raion" title="Raion">raion</a></i>), three municipalities and two <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_territorial_unit" title="Autonomous territorial unit">autonomous regions</a> (<a href="/wiki/Gagauzia" title="Gagauzia">Gagauzia</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Administrative-Territorial_Units_of_the_Left_Bank_of_the_Dniester" title="Administrative-Territorial Units of the Left Bank of the Dniester">Left Bank of the Dniester</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223">&#91;218&#93;</a></sup> The final status of Transnistria is <a href="/wiki/Disputed_status_of_Transnistria" class="mw-redirect" title="Disputed status of Transnistria">disputed</a>, as the central government does not control that territory. 10 other cities, including <a href="/wiki/Comrat" title="Comrat">Comrat</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tiraspol" title="Tiraspol">Tiraspol</a>, the administrative seats of the two autonomous territories, also have <a href="/wiki/Municipiu" title="Municipiu">municipality status</a>.
</p><p>Moldova has 66 cities (towns), including 13 with municipality status, and 916 communes. Another 700 villages are too small to have a separate administration and are administratively part of either cities (41 of them) or communes (659). This makes for a total of 1,682 localities in Moldova, two of which are uninhabited.<sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224">&#91;219&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The largest city in Moldova is Chișinău with a population of approx. 695,400 people. The second largest city is Tiraspol at 129,500, part of the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_with_limited_recognition" title="List of states with limited recognition">unrecognised breakaway region</a> of <a href="/wiki/Transnistria" title="Transnistria">Transnistria</a>, followed by Bălți (146,900) and Bender (91,000).
</p>

<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Law_enforcement_and_emergency_services">Law enforcement and emergency services</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Crime_in_Moldova" title="Crime in Moldova">Crime in Moldova</a> and <a href="/wiki/Healthcare_in_Moldova" title="Healthcare in Moldova">Healthcare in Moldova</a></div><p>The Moldovan police force (<a href="/wiki/Moldovan_Police" title="Moldovan Police">General Police Inspectorate</a>) reports to the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Internal_Affairs_(Moldova)" title="Ministry of Internal Affairs (Moldova)">Ministry of Internal Affairs</a> (MAI) and is the primary law enforcement body, responsible for internal security, public order, traffic, and criminal investigations. Several agencies responsible for border management, emergency situations, migration and asylum also report to the ministry. Civilian authorities maintained effective control over the security forces.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_220-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-220">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup> The Moldovan Police are divided into state and municipal organisations. State police provide law enforcement throughout Moldova while municipal police operate at the local <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Moldova" title="Administrative divisions of Moldova">administrative</a> level. National and municipal police forces often collaborate closely for law enforcement purposes. The <a href="/wiki/Special_Forces_Brigade_%22Fulger%22" title="Special Forces Brigade &quot;Fulger&quot;">Special Forces Brigade "Fulger"</a> is a specialized combat-ready police force primarily responsible for tackling organized crime, serious violent crime, and hostage situations. They are subordinate to the General Police Inspectorate and therefore under strict civilian control.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_220-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-220">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>There are also a number of more specialised police institutions including the Police Department of Chisinau Municipality and the General Directorate of Criminal Investigation. The <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_Border_Police" title="Moldovan Border Police">Moldovan Border Police</a> are responsible for border security. It was a military branch until 2012 when it was put under the control of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. According to <i>The Law on Police Use of Force Worldwide,</i> "Moldova does not regulate and restrict the use of firearms by law enforcement officials as international law requires. Police use of a firearm can only be lawful where necessary to confront an imminent threat of death or serious injury or a grave and proximate threat to life."<sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225">&#91;220&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Security_and_Intelligence_Service_of_Moldova" title="Security and Intelligence Service of Moldova">Security and Intelligence Service</a> (SIS) is a Moldovan state body specialized in ensuring <a href="/wiki/National_security" title="National security">national security</a> by exercising all appropriate <a href="/wiki/Intelligence_analysis" title="Intelligence analysis">intelligence</a> and <a href="/wiki/Counterintelligence" title="Counterintelligence">counter-intelligence</a> measures, such as: collecting, processing, checking and capitalizing the information needed to identify, prevent and counteract any actions that according to law represent an internal or external threat to <a href="/wiki/Independence" title="Independence">independence</a>, sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity, constitutional order, democratic development, internal security of the state, society and citizens, the statehood of the Republic of Moldova, the stable functioning of vitally important branches of the national economy, both on the territory of the Republic of Moldova and abroad.
</p><p>Emergency services in Moldova consist of <a href="/wiki/Emergency_medical_services" title="Emergency medical services">emergency medical services</a>, <a href="/wiki/Search_and_rescue" title="Search and rescue">search and rescue</a> units, and a state <a href="/wiki/Firefighting" title="Firefighting">firefighting service</a>. There are two hospitals in the capital city Chișinău, the primary being Medpark International Hospital, and general hospitals in <a href="/wiki/B%C4%83l%C8%9Bi" title="Bălți">Bălți</a>, <a href="/wiki/Briceni" title="Briceni">Briceni</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cahul" title="Cahul">Cahul</a>, and <a href="/wiki/C%C4%83l%C4%83ra%C8%99i,_Moldova" title="Călărași, Moldova">Călărași</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup> Moldova has a universal healthcare system through a <a href="/wiki/Mandatory_health_insurance" class="mw-redirect" title="Mandatory health insurance">mandatory health insurance</a> scheme. Casa Mariorei, founded in 2002, is a <a href="/wiki/Women%27s_shelter" title="Women&#39;s shelter">domestic violence shelter</a> in Chișinău which provides shelter, healthcare, legal advice, and psychosocial support for native Moldovan, immigrant, and refugee women.<sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Geography">Geography</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Geography_of_Moldova" title="Geography of Moldova">Geography of Moldova</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Malul_abrupt_al_Nistrului_Naslavcea-Verejeni_Ocnita_(11).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Malul_abrupt_al_Nistrului_Naslavcea-Verejeni_Ocnita_%2811%29.jpg/220px-Malul_abrupt_al_Nistrului_Naslavcea-Verejeni_Ocnita_%2811%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Malul_abrupt_al_Nistrului_Naslavcea-Verejeni_Ocnita_%2811%29.jpg/330px-Malul_abrupt_al_Nistrului_Naslavcea-Verejeni_Ocnita_%2811%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Malul_abrupt_al_Nistrului_Naslavcea-Verejeni_Ocnita_%2811%29.jpg/440px-Malul_abrupt_al_Nistrului_Naslavcea-Verejeni_Ocnita_%2811%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1440" data-file-height="965" /></a><figcaption>Scenery in Moldova, with <a href="/wiki/Dniester_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Dniester River">Dniester River</a></figcaption></figure><p>Moldova is a landlocked country situated in Eastern Europe, on the northeastern corner of the <a href="/wiki/Balkans" title="Balkans">Balkans</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea_Basin" class="mw-redirect" title="Black Sea Basin">Black Sea Basin</a>, between latitudes <a href="/wiki/45th_parallel_north" title="45th parallel north">45°</a> and <a href="/wiki/49th_parallel_north" title="49th parallel north">49° N</a>, and mostly between meridians <a href="/wiki/26th_meridian_east" title="26th meridian east">26°</a> and <a href="/wiki/30th_meridian_east" title="30th meridian east">30° E</a> (a small area lies east of 30°). The country lies to the east of the <a href="/wiki/Carpathian_Mountains" title="Carpathian Mountains">Carpathian Mountains</a> and is bordered by <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a> to its west and by <a href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</a> to its north, east, and south. The total length of the national boundaries is 1,389 km, including 939 km with Ukraine and 450 km with Romania. The country is separated from Romania on the west by the <a href="/wiki/Prut" title="Prut">Prut</a> river and on the east from Ukraine by the <a href="/wiki/Dniester" title="Dniester">Dniester</a> river. The total land area is 33,843.5 <a href="/wiki/Square_kilometre" title="Square kilometre">km<sup>2</sup></a> (13,067 <a href="/wiki/Square_mile" title="Square mile">sq mi</a>), of which 960 km<sup>2</sup> (370 sq mi) is water. The largest part of the country (around 88% of the area) lies in the <a href="/wiki/Bessarabia" title="Bessarabia">Bessarabia</a> region, while a narrow strip in the east is located in the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_with_limited_recognition" title="List of states with limited recognition">unrecognised breakaway state</a> of <a href="/wiki/Transnistria" title="Transnistria">Transnistria</a> on the eastern bank of the Dniester.
</p><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Moldova_-_landscape_in_H%C3%AEnce%C8%99ti_District_02.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Moldova_-_landscape_in_H%C3%AEnce%C8%99ti_District_02.jpg/220px-Moldova_-_landscape_in_H%C3%AEnce%C8%99ti_District_02.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Moldova_-_landscape_in_H%C3%AEnce%C8%99ti_District_02.jpg/330px-Moldova_-_landscape_in_H%C3%AEnce%C8%99ti_District_02.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Moldova_-_landscape_in_H%C3%AEnce%C8%99ti_District_02.jpg/440px-Moldova_-_landscape_in_H%C3%AEnce%C8%99ti_District_02.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3208" data-file-height="2139" /></a><figcaption>Moldovan landscape in the <a href="/wiki/H%C3%AEnce%C8%99ti_District" title="Hîncești District">Hîncești District</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Although the country is technically landlocked, the <a href="/wiki/Port_of_Giurgiule%C8%99ti" title="Port of Giurgiulești">port</a> of <a href="/wiki/Giurgiule%C8%99ti" title="Giurgiulești">Giurgiulești</a> in the extreme south-west of the country lies on the confluence of the <a href="/wiki/Danube" title="Danube">Danube</a> and Prut rivers, which therefore provides it with access to <a href="/wiki/International_waters" title="International waters">international waters</a> through the Danube which empties into the <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a>. The Dniester river, which rises in Ukraine near the city of <a href="/wiki/Drohobych" title="Drohobych">Drohobych</a>, passes through Moldova, separating the main territory from its unrecognised breakaway region Transnistria, and empties into the Black Sea in Ukraine. At its closest point, Moldova is separated from the <a href="/wiki/Dniester_Liman" class="mw-redirect" title="Dniester Liman">Dniester Liman</a>, an estuary of the Black Sea, by only 3 km of Ukrainian territory.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Moldova_Competitiveness_Project,_USAID_Moldova_(48121769796).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Moldova_Competitiveness_Project%2C_USAID_Moldova_%2848121769796%29.jpg/220px-Moldova_Competitiveness_Project%2C_USAID_Moldova_%2848121769796%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="124" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Moldova_Competitiveness_Project%2C_USAID_Moldova_%2848121769796%29.jpg/330px-Moldova_Competitiveness_Project%2C_USAID_Moldova_%2848121769796%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Moldova_Competitiveness_Project%2C_USAID_Moldova_%2848121769796%29.jpg/440px-Moldova_Competitiveness_Project%2C_USAID_Moldova_%2848121769796%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5464" data-file-height="3070" /></a><figcaption>Dniester River, Moldova.</figcaption></figure>
<p>While most of the country is hilly, elevations never exceed 430 m (1,411 ft), the highest point being the <a href="/wiki/Dealul_B%C4%83l%C4%83ne%C8%99ti" class="mw-redirect" title="Dealul Bălănești">Bălănești Hill</a>. Moldova's hills are part of the <a href="/wiki/Moldavian_Plateau" title="Moldavian Plateau">Moldavian Plateau</a>, which geologically originate from the Carpathian Mountains. Its subdivisions in Moldova include the Dniester Hills (Northern Moldavian Hills and Dniester Ridge), the Moldavian Plain (Middle Prut Valley and <a href="/wiki/B%C4%83l%C8%9Bi_Steppe" title="Bălți Steppe">Bălți Steppe</a>), and the Central Moldavian Plateau (Ciuluc-Soloneț Hills, Cornești Hills—<a href="/wiki/Codri" class="mw-redirect" title="Codri">Codri</a> Massive, "Codri" meaning "forests"—Lower Dniester Hills, Lower Prut Valley, and Tigheci Hills). In the south, the country has a small flatland, the <a href="/wiki/Bugeac_Plain" class="mw-redirect" title="Bugeac Plain">Bugeac Plain</a>. The territory of Moldova east of the river Dniester is split between parts of the <a href="/wiki/Podolian_Plateau" class="mw-redirect" title="Podolian Plateau">Podolian Plateau</a>, and parts of the <a href="/wiki/Eurasian_Steppe" title="Eurasian Steppe">Eurasian Steppe</a>. Moldova's exceptionally rich <a href="/wiki/Chernozem" title="Chernozem">Chernozem</a> soil covers around three-quarters of the country's land area.<sup id="cite_ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Moldova's capital and largest city is <a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Chișinău">Chișinău</a>, with approximately a third of the country's population residing in its metro area. Chișinău is Moldova's main industrial and commercial centre, and is located in the middle of the country, on the river <a href="/wiki/B%C3%AEc" title="Bîc">Bîc</a>, a tributary of the <a href="/wiki/Dniester" title="Dniester">Dniester</a>. Moldova's second-largest city is <a href="/wiki/Tiraspol" title="Tiraspol">Tiraspol</a>, which lies on the eastern bank of the Dniester and is the capital of the <a href="/wiki/List_of_states_with_limited_recognition" title="List of states with limited recognition">unrecognised breakaway region</a> of <a href="/wiki/Transnistria" title="Transnistria">Transnistria</a>. The country's third-largest city is <a href="/wiki/B%C4%83l%C8%9Bi" title="Bălți">Bălți</a>, often referred to as the 'northern capital'. It is situated 127 kilometres (79 mi) north of the capital Chișinău, and is located on the river <a href="/wiki/R%C4%83ut_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Răut River">Răut</a>, a tributary of the Dniester, on a hilly landscape in the Bălți steppe. <a href="/wiki/Comrat" title="Comrat">Comrat</a> is the administrative centre of the <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_region" class="mw-redirect" title="Autonomous region">autonomous region</a> of <a href="/wiki/Gagauzia" title="Gagauzia">Gagauzia</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Climate">Climate</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Orhei_Vechi,_Moldova_-_Flickr_-_Dave_Proffer_(13).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Orhei_Vechi%2C_Moldova_-_Flickr_-_Dave_Proffer_%2813%29.jpg/220px-Orhei_Vechi%2C_Moldova_-_Flickr_-_Dave_Proffer_%2813%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Orhei_Vechi%2C_Moldova_-_Flickr_-_Dave_Proffer_%2813%29.jpg/330px-Orhei_Vechi%2C_Moldova_-_Flickr_-_Dave_Proffer_%2813%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Orhei_Vechi%2C_Moldova_-_Flickr_-_Dave_Proffer_%2813%29.jpg/440px-Orhei_Vechi%2C_Moldova_-_Flickr_-_Dave_Proffer_%2813%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3264" data-file-height="2448" /></a><figcaption>Cave churches at <a href="/wiki/Old_Orhei" title="Old Orhei">Old Orhei</a>, part of the <a href="/wiki/Protected_areas_of_Moldova" title="Protected areas of Moldova">only national park</a> in the country</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Toltre_FT%C8%98T-52.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Toltre_FT%C8%98T-52.JPG/220px-Toltre_FT%C8%98T-52.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Toltre_FT%C8%98T-52.JPG/330px-Toltre_FT%C8%98T-52.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Toltre_FT%C8%98T-52.JPG/440px-Toltre_FT%C8%98T-52.JPG 2x" data-file-width="4320" data-file-height="3240" /></a><figcaption>Toltrele Prutului near <a href="/wiki/Fete%C8%99ti,_Edine%C8%9B" title="Fetești, Edineț">Fetești</a>, <a href="/wiki/Edine%C8%9B_District" title="Edineț District">Edineț District</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Moldova has a climate which is moderately continental; its proximity to the <a href="/wiki/Black_Sea" title="Black Sea">Black Sea</a> leads to the climate being mildly cold in the autumn and winter and relatively cool in the spring and summer.<sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The summers are warm and long, with temperatures averaging about 20&#160;°C (68&#160;°F) and the winters are relatively mild and dry, with January temperatures averaging −4&#160;°C (25&#160;°F). Annual rainfall, which ranges from around 600&#160;mm (24&#160;in) in the north to 400&#160;mm (16&#160;in) in the south, can vary greatly; long dry spells are not unusual. The heaviest rainfall occurs in early summer and again in October; heavy showers and thunderstorms are common. Because of the irregular terrain, heavy summer rains often cause erosion and river silting.
</p><p>The highest temperature ever recorded in Moldova was 41.5&#160;°C (106.7&#160;°F) on 21 July 2007 in <a href="/wiki/Camenca" title="Camenca">Camenca</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-231" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-231">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup> The lowest temperature ever recorded was −35.5&#160;°C (−31.9&#160;°F) on 20 January 1963 in Brătușeni, Edineț county.<sup id="cite_ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Biodiversity">Biodiversity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Protected_areas_in_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="Protected areas in Moldova">Protected areas in Moldova</a></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Phytogeography" title="Phytogeography">Phytogeographically</a>, Moldova is split between the <a href="/wiki/East_European_Plain" title="East European Plain">East European Plain</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Pontic%E2%80%93Caspian_steppe" title="Pontic–Caspian steppe">Pontic–Caspian steppe</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Circumboreal_Region" title="Circumboreal Region">Circumboreal Region</a> within the <a href="/wiki/Boreal_Kingdom" title="Boreal Kingdom">Boreal Kingdom</a>. It is home to three terrestrial ecoregions: <a href="/wiki/Central_European_mixed_forests" title="Central European mixed forests">Central European mixed forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/East_European_forest_steppe" title="East European forest steppe">East European forest steppe</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Pontic_steppe" class="mw-redirect" title="Pontic steppe">Pontic steppe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-DinersteinOlson2017_234-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-234">&#91;229&#93;</a></sup> Forests currently cover only 11% of Moldova, though the state is making efforts to increase their range. It had a 2019 <a href="/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index" title="Forest Landscape Integrity Index">Forest Landscape Integrity Index</a> mean score of 2.2/10, ranking it 158th globally out of 172 countries.<sup id="cite_ref-FLII-Supplementary_235-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-235">&#91;230&#93;</a></sup> Game animals, such as <a href="/wiki/Red_deer" title="Red deer">red deer</a>, <a href="/wiki/Roe_deer" title="Roe deer">roe deer</a> and <a href="/wiki/Wild_boar" title="Wild boar">wild boar</a> can be found in these wooded areas.<sup id="cite_ref-Environmental_issues_in_Moldova_236-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Environmental_issues_in_Moldova-236">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup></p><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Saiga_antelope_at_the_Stepnoi_Sanctuary.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Saiga_antelope_at_the_Stepnoi_Sanctuary.jpg/220px-Saiga_antelope_at_the_Stepnoi_Sanctuary.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="186" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/Saiga_antelope_at_the_Stepnoi_Sanctuary.jpg/330px-Saiga_antelope_at_the_Stepnoi_Sanctuary.jpg 1.5x, /></a><figcaption>Noted for its vivid portrayal of the lower <a href="/wiki/Dniester_river" class="mw-redirect" title="Dniester river">Dniester river</a>, <a href="/wiki/Henryk_Sienkiewicz" title="Henryk Sienkiewicz">Henryk Sienkiewicz</a>'s novel <i><a href="/wiki/With_Fire_and_Sword" title="With Fire and Sword">With Fire and Sword</a></i> opens with a description of <a class="mw-redirect" title="Critically endangered">critically endangered</a> <a href="/wiki/Species" title="Species">species</a> that is now extinct in Moldova.</figcaption></figure>

<p>The environment of Moldova suffered extreme degradation during the Soviet period, when industrial and agricultural development proceeded without regard for environmental protection.<sup id="cite_ref-Environmental_issues_in_Moldova_236-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Environmental_issues_in_Moldova-236">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> Excessive use of pesticides resulted in heavily polluted topsoil, and industries lacked emission controls.<sup id="cite_ref-Environmental_issues_in_Moldova_236-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Environmental_issues_in_Moldova-236">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> Founded in 1990, the <a href="/wiki/Ecological_Movement_of_Moldova" title="Ecological Movement of Moldova">Ecological Movement of Moldova</a>, a national, non-governmental, nonprofit organization which is a member of the <a href="/wiki/International_Union_for_Conservation_of_Nature" title="International Union for Conservation of Nature">International Union for Conservation of Nature</a> has been working to restore Moldova's damaged natural environment.<sup id="cite_ref-Environmental_issues_in_Moldova_236-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Environmental_issues_in_Moldova-236">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> The movement is national representative of the Center "Naturopa" of the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a> and <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Environment_Programme" title="United Nations Environment Programme">United Nations Environment Programme</a> of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239">&#91;234&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Once possessing a range from the <a href="/wiki/British_Isles" title="British Isles">British Isles</a> through <a href="/wiki/Central_Asia" title="Central Asia">Central Asia</a> over the <a href="/wiki/Bering_Strait" title="Bering Strait">Bering Strait</a> into <a href="/wiki/Alaska" title="Alaska">Alaska</a> and Canada's <a href="/wiki/Yukon" title="Yukon">Yukon</a> as well as the <a href="/wiki/Northwest_Territories" title="Northwest Territories">Northwest Territories</a>, <a href="/wiki/Saiga_antelope" title="Saiga antelope">saigas</a> survived in Moldova and Romania into the late 18th century. Deforestation, demographic pressure, as well as excessive hunting eradicated the native saiga herds which is <a href="/wiki/Critically_endangered" class="mw-redirect" title="Critically endangered">currently threatened with extinction</a>. They were considered a characteristic animal of <a href="/wiki/Scythia" title="Scythia">Scythia</a> in antiquity. Historian <a href="/wiki/Strabo" title="Strabo">Strabo</a> referred to the saigas as the <i>kolos</i>, describing it as "between the deer and ram in size" which (understandably but wrongly) was believed to drink through its nose.<sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240">&#91;235&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Another animal which was extinct in Moldova since the 18th century until recently was the European Wood Bison or <a href="/wiki/Wisent" class="mw-redirect" title="Wisent">wisent</a>. The species was reintroduced with the arrival of three European bison from <a href="/wiki/Bia%C5%82owie%C5%BCa_Forest" title="Białowieża Forest">Białowieża Forest</a> in Poland several days before <a href="/wiki/Independence_Day_of_the_Republic_of_Moldova" title="Independence Day of the Republic of Moldova">Moldova's Independence Day</a> on 27 August 2005.<sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241">&#91;236&#93;</a></sup> Moldova is currently interested in expanding their wisent population, and began talks with Belarus in 2019 regarding a bison exchange program between the two countries.<sup id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Economy">Economy</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Moldova" title="Economy of Moldova">Economy of Moldova</a></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Overview">Overview</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Annual_growth_of_GDP_for_Moldova,_Romania,_and_Ukraine,_1980_to_2028.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Annual_growth_of_GDP_for_Moldova%2C_Romania%2C_and_Ukraine%2C_1980_to_2028.svg/220px-Annual_growth_of_GDP_for_Moldova%2C_Romania%2C_and_Ukraine%2C_1980_to_2028.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="155" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Annual_growth_of_GDP_for_Moldova%2C_Romania%2C_and_Ukraine%2C_1980_to_2028.svg/330px-Annual_growth_of_GDP_for_Moldova%2C_Romania%2C_and_Ukraine%2C_1980_to_2028.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Annual_growth_of_GDP_for_Moldova%2C_Romania%2C_and_Ukraine%2C_1980_to_2028.svg/440px-Annual_growth_of_GDP_for_Moldova%2C_Romania%2C_and_Ukraine%2C_1980_to_2028.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="850" data-file-height="600" /></a><figcaption>Annual growth of <a href="/wiki/Gross_domestic_product" title="Gross domestic product">GDP</a> for <a class="mw-selflink selflink">Moldova</a>, <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</a>, 1980 to 2028</figcaption></figure>
<p>The economy of Moldova is an <a href="/wiki/Emerging_market" title="Emerging market">emerging</a> upper-middle income economy, with a high <a href="/wiki/Human_Development_Index" title="Human Development Index">Human Development Index</a>. Since the country gained <a href="/wiki/Independence_Day_of_the_Republic_of_Moldova" title="Independence Day of the Republic of Moldova">independence</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Soviet_Union" title="Soviet Union">Soviet Union</a> in 1992, it has steadily transitioned to a <a href="/wiki/Market_economy" title="Market economy">market economy</a>. According to the <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>, despite a strong economic performance over the past two decades, Moldova remains among the poorest nations in Europe. Growth has remained relatively high since the 1990s, with low levels of unemployment and falling levels of poverty, but a combination of demographic factors, especially an <a href="/wiki/Population_ageing" title="Population ageing">ageing population</a> and significant levels of <a href="/wiki/Emigration" title="Emigration">emigration</a>, and recent regional events, especially <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russia's invasion of Ukraine</a>, have posed serious economic challenges to the Moldovan economy, particularly due to inflation and rising energy prices. Productivity growth has remained poor, and a significant proportion of the population are reliant on government pensions and social assistance.<sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup> Due to Moldova's historic reliance upon Russian oil and natural gas, the energy sector has posed a particular challenge to the country's economy. 
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:GDP_Per_Capita_North_Balkan_Region.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/GDP_Per_Capita_North_Balkan_Region.svg/220px-GDP_Per_Capita_North_Balkan_Region.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="155" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/GDP_Per_Capita_North_Balkan_Region.svg/330px-GDP_Per_Capita_North_Balkan_Region.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/GDP_Per_Capita_North_Balkan_Region.svg/440px-GDP_Per_Capita_North_Balkan_Region.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="850" data-file-height="600" /></a><figcaption>Real GDP per capita development of <a class="mw-selflink selflink">Moldova</a>, <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Measures_of_national_income_and_output" title="Measures of national income and output">GDP per capita</a> has almost doubled from $2,749 (USD) in 2015 to $5,562 in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup> Following the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent lockdowns, annual GDP growth rebounded to 13.9% in 2021, before Russia's invasion of Ukraine, energy and refugee crises caused growth to collapse to −5.9%. As of 2022, unemployment remains low at 2.3%, but inflation had dramatically increased to 28.7% due to the energy crisis caused by the invasion.<sup id="cite_ref-245" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-245">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> In recent years the country has received significant economic assistance from the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a>, IMF, and World Bank, particularly after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">IMF</a> predicts that in 2023 the economy will improve from a 1.5% contraction to a growth of 1.5%.<sup id="cite_ref-246" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-246">&#91;241&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Moldova remains highly vulnerable to fluctuations in <a href="/wiki/Remittance" title="Remittance">remittances</a> from workers abroad (which constitute 25 percent of GDP), exports to the <a href="/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Independent_States" title="Commonwealth of Independent States">Commonwealth of Independent States</a> (CIS) and <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> (EU) (88 per cent of total exports), and donor support (about 10 per cent of government spending).<sup id="cite_ref-:0_247-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-247">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup> The main transmission channels through which adverse exogenous shocks could impact the Moldovan economy are remittances (also due to potentially returning migrants), external trade, and capital flows.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_247-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-247">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The economy's primary exports are agriculture, apparel, and sports equipments.<sup id="cite_ref-248" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-248">&#91;243&#93;</a></sup> In 2021, Moldova exported $140 million in wine and is the 21st largest exporter of wine in the world, with wine exports being the country's fifth largest export.<sup id="cite_ref-249" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-249">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup> With its 300 days of sunshine per year, the climate in Moldova is ideal for agriculture and particularly <a href="/wiki/Vineyard" title="Vineyard">vineyards</a>. The wine industry is a major economic sector, representing three percent of Moldova's GDP and eight percent of the country's total exports, according to government data.<sup id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-250">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup> In 2021, the EU became the main purchaser of Moldovan wines. <a href="/wiki/Information_and_communications_technology" title="Information and communications technology">Information and Communication Technology</a> (ICT) is one of the most promising economic sectors in Moldova, accounting for more than 10 percent of GDP. More than 2,000 students graduate with a degree in computing or a related field per year.<sup id="cite_ref-251" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-251">&#91;246&#93;</a></sup> IT companies export about 80 percent of their total production to the <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</a>, the <a href="/wiki/United_Kingdom" title="United Kingdom">United Kingdom</a>, <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a>, <a href="/wiki/Germany" title="Germany">Germany</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Netherlands" title="Netherlands">Netherlands</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a>. 
</p>
