<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Energy">Energy</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Energy_in_Moldova" title="Energy in Moldova">Energy in Moldova</a></div>
<p>With few natural energy resources, Moldova imports almost all of its energy supplies. 50% of the country's national energy company, Moldovagaz, is owned by Russian oil and natural gas supplier <a href="/wiki/Gazprom" title="Gazprom">Gazprom</a>, the remaining 36% split between the Moldovan government (36.6%) and the unrecognised government of Transnistria (13.4%).<sup id="cite_ref-253" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-253">&#91;248&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-254" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-254">&#91;249&#93;</a></sup> Moldova's historic dependence on Russian energy is underscored by a debt of more than US$709 million to Gazprom as well as a further US$7 billion by Transnistria. Russia supplies the breakaway pro-Russian region with oil and natural gas without requiring them to pay, with the cost levied as debt against the Moldovan state as a form of economic warfare.<sup id="cite_ref-255" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-255">&#91;250&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-256" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-256">&#91;251&#93;</a></sup> The Moldovan government disputes the figures, and has identified more than US$100 million in fraudulent claims by Gazprom.<sup id="cite_ref-257" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-257">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>In August 2013, work began on a new pipeline between Moldova and Romania that has now been completed and has broken Russia's monopoly on Moldova's gas supplies.<sup id="cite_ref-indexmundi.com_258-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-indexmundi.com-258">&#91;253&#93;</a></sup> Importing electricity from Romania began in 2022, breaking the need to buy electricity produced from Russian gas in Transnistria. Improved connectivity will be completed by 2025<sup id="cite_ref-259" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-259">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup> As of May 2023, Moldova no longer imports oil or natural gas from Russia and has been granted access to the European Union's joint gas purchasing platform.<sup id="cite_ref-260" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-260">&#91;255&#93;</a></sup> Financial assistance was provided by the European Union, World Bank, and IMF in order to speed up this transition.<sup id="cite_ref-261" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-261">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-262" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-262">&#91;257&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Tourism">Tourism</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Tourism_in_Moldova" title="Tourism in Moldova">Tourism in Moldova</a></div>
<p>Moldova is the among least visited country in Europe, and tourism consequently plays a relatively minor role in the country's overall economy.<sup id="cite_ref-263" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-263">&#91;258&#93;</a></sup> Despite the impact of <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russia's invasion of neighbouring Ukraine</a>, Moldova saw more foreign visitors in the first quarter of 2022 than pre-<a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic" title="COVID-19 pandemic">pandemic</a>, going from 31,000 non-resident tourists in 2019 to 36,100 in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-264" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-264">&#91;259&#93;</a></sup> This still makes it one of the least-visited countries in Europe, however in recent years a number of Western media outlets have begun to highlight Moldova and its capital city <a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Chișinău">Chișinău</a> as an attractive tourism destination due to its picturesque natural landscapes, 300 days of sunshine per year, low prices, ancient wine culture, and mix of regional cultural influences.<sup id="cite_ref-265" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-265">&#91;260&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-266" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-266">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-267" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-267">&#91;262&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-268" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-268">&#91;263&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-269" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-269">&#91;264&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-270" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-270">&#91;265&#93;</a></sup> Tourism in Moldova has focused on the country's natural landscapes, historical sites, and historic wine tradition. The government promotes international tourism within the country through its Moldova Travel brand.<sup id="cite_ref-271" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-271">&#91;266&#93;</a></sup> Moldova is internationally connected by plane via <a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u_International_Airport" title="Chișinău International Airport">Chișinău International Airport</a>, with direct flights to and from many European destinations, including <a href="/wiki/Amsterdam_Airport_Schiphol" title="Amsterdam Airport Schiphol">Amsterdam Schiphol</a>, <a href="/wiki/Berlin_Brandenburg_Airport" title="Berlin Brandenburg Airport">Berlin Brandenburg</a>, <a href="/wiki/London_Stansted_Airport" title="London Stansted Airport">London Stansted</a>, <a href="/wiki/Charles_de_Gaulle_Airport" title="Charles de Gaulle Airport">Paris–Charles de Gaulle</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv" title="Tel Aviv">Tel Aviv</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Ben_Gurion_Airport" title="Ben Gurion Airport">Ben Gurion Airport</a>, <a href="/wiki/Leonardo_da_Vinci%E2%80%93Fiumicino_Airport" title="Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino Airport">Rome–Fiumicino Airport</a>, <a href="/wiki/Istanbul_Airport" title="Istanbul Airport">Istanbul Airport</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Dubai_International_Airport" title="Dubai International Airport">Dubai International Airport</a>. Rail links connect it via direct overnight trains to neighbouring <a href="/wiki/Bucharest" title="Bucharest">Bucharest</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kyiv" title="Kyiv">Kyiv</a>, <a href="/wiki/Odesa" title="Odesa">Odesa</a>, and formerly <a href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_272-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-272">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup> Moldovan citizens also enjoy visa-free travel across the <a href="/wiki/Schengen_Area" title="Schengen Area">Schengen Area</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_273-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-273">&#91;268&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Orhei_Moldova.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Orhei_Moldova.jpg/220px-Orhei_Moldova.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Orhei_Moldova.jpg/330px-Orhei_Moldova.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5e/Orhei_Moldova.jpg/440px-Orhei_Moldova.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5184" data-file-height="3456" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Orhei_National_Park" title="Orhei National Park">Orhei National Park</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>As a major exporter of wine with more than 142 wineries and the largest wine cellar in the world, vineyard tours are offered to tourists across the country. Major sites include the <a href="/wiki/Cricova_(winery)" title="Cricova (winery)">Cricova</a> winery, whose wine cellar stretches more than 120 kilometres (75 miles); <a href="/wiki/Mimi_Castle" title="Mimi Castle">Castel Mimi</a>, a 19th-century chateau with vineyards, a museum, art gallery, spa, hotel, and restaurant; and <a href="/wiki/Mile%C8%99tii_Mici_(winery)" title="Mileștii Mici (winery)">Mileștii Mici</a>, which boasts the world's largest collection of wine.<sup id="cite_ref-:4_274-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-274">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup> As a country with a deep history of <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Christianity" class="mw-redirect" title="Eastern Orthodox Christianity">Eastern Orthodox Christianity</a>, the country also has more than 50 monasteries and 700 churches.<sup id="cite_ref-275" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-275">&#91;270&#93;</a></sup> Among the most famous and well-visited are the <a href="/wiki/Old_Orhei" title="Old Orhei">Old Orhei</a> <a href="/wiki/List_of_cave_monasteries" title="List of cave monasteries">Cave Monastery</a>, carved into a cliff face in the 13th century and still in use today, and the 19th century <a href="/wiki/Nativity_Cathedral,_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Nativity Cathedral, Chișinău">Nativity Cathedral</a> in the centre of Chișinău. <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> includes both the Old Orhei Archaeological Landscape, which features evidence of settlements dating back to at least the 12th century, and the typical <a href="/wiki/Chernozem" title="Chernozem">Chernozem</a> soil on the <a href="/wiki/B%C4%83l%C8%9Bi_Steppe" title="Bălți Steppe">Bălți Steppe</a> of Moldova (the most arable soil on the planet) on its Tentative List of <a href="/wiki/World_Heritage_Site" title="World Heritage Site">World Heritage Sites</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-276" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-276">&#91;271&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-277" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-277">&#91;272&#93;</a></sup> The capital city of <a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Chișinău">Chișinău</a> hosts most of the country's national museums, including the <a href="/wiki/National_Museum_of_Fine_Arts,_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="National Museum of Fine Arts, Chișinău">National Museum of Fine Arts</a>, <a href="/wiki/Moldova_State_University" title="Moldova State University">Moldova State University</a>, Brancusi Gallery, the <a href="/wiki/National_Museum_of_History_of_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="National Museum of History of Moldova">National Museum of History of Moldova</a> with over 236,000 exhibits, as well as bustling markets in the north of the city, including the house where <a href="/wiki/Alexander_Pushkin" title="Alexander Pushkin">Alexander Pushkin</a> once resided while in exile from the <a href="/wiki/Tsar" title="Tsar">Russian Tsar</a>, and which has since been turned into a museum. Every year on October 3–4, the country celebrates National Wine Day, where wine producers open up their wineries to the general public and provide shuttle buses between locations.<sup id="cite_ref-278" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-278">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Wine_industry">Wine industry</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_wine" title="Moldovan wine">Moldovan wine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Mile%C5%9Ftii_Mici_(3944427747).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Mile%C5%9Ftii_Mici_%283944427747%29.jpg/220px-Mile%C5%9Ftii_Mici_%283944427747%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Mile%C5%9Ftii_Mici_%283944427747%29.jpg/330px-Mile%C5%9Ftii_Mici_%283944427747%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Mile%C5%9Ftii_Mici_%283944427747%29.jpg/440px-Mile%C5%9Ftii_Mici_%283944427747%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3264" data-file-height="2448" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Mile%C8%99tii_Mici" title="Mileștii Mici">Mileștii Mici</a> is home to the world's biggest <a href="/wiki/Wine_cellar" title="Wine cellar">wine cellar</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>With its 300 days of sunshine per year, the climate in Moldova is ideal for agriculture and particularly <a href="/wiki/Vineyard" title="Vineyard">vineyards</a>. The wine industry is a major economic sector, representing three percent of Moldova's GDP and eight percent of the country's total exports, according to government data. Moldovan wine is being exported into over 70 states worldwide. Although Moldova is barely larger than <a href="/wiki/Belgium" title="Belgium">Belgium</a>, the country has 122,000 hectares of vineyards and is among the 20 largest producers in the world, according to a report by the <a href="/wiki/International_Organisation_of_Vine_and_Wine" title="International Organisation of Vine and Wine">International Organisation of Vine and Wine</a> (OIV).<sup id="cite_ref-279" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-279">&#91;274&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Before <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russia's invasion of Ukraine</a> and Moldova's pivot towards Europe, a majority of its wine exports went to Russia, but this has now changed: "Russia accounted for only 10 percent of Moldovan wine exports in 2021, down from 80 percent in the early 2000s, according to figures from the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Agriculture_and_Food_Industry_(Moldova)" title="Ministry of Agriculture and Food Industry (Moldova)">Moldovan Ministry of Agriculture</a>."<sup id="cite_ref-:06_280-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:06-280">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup> The EU liberalized its market for Moldovan wines and has signed a bilateral free trade deal with Moldova, with the result that in 2021 the country exported more than 120 million litres of wine to European countries, compared to 8.6 million litres to Russia.<sup id="cite_ref-:06_280-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:06-280">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Many families have their own recipes and <a href="/wiki/Grape_varieties" class="mw-redirect" title="Grape varieties">grape varieties</a> that have been passed down through the generations. There are 3 historical wine regions: Valul lui Traian (south west), Stefan Voda (south east) and <a href="/wiki/Codru_(wine)" title="Codru (wine)">Codru</a> (center), destined for the production of wines with protected geographic indication.<sup id="cite_ref-natura2000_22-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-natura2000-22">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Mile%C8%99tii_Mici_(winery)" title="Mileștii Mici (winery)">Mileștii Mici</a> is the home of the largest wine cellar in the world. It stretches for 200&#160;km (120&#160;mi) (though only 55&#160;km (34&#160;mi) is in use) and holds some 2 million or more bottles of wine.<sup id="cite_ref-281" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-281">&#91;276&#93;</a></sup> It has retained the <a href="/wiki/Guinness_World_Records" title="Guinness World Records">Guinness World Record</a> for largest wine cellar by number of bottles since 2005.<sup id="cite_ref-:4_274-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-274">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup> The earliest wines in its collection date to 1969. <a href="/wiki/Mimi_Castle" title="Mimi Castle">Mimi Castle</a> in the south east is a winery and <a href="/wiki/Cultural_property" title="Cultural property">architectural monument</a>, which was built at the end of the 19th century in the village of <a href="/wiki/Bulboaca,_Anenii_Noi" title="Bulboaca, Anenii Noi">Bulboaca</a> in the district <a href="/wiki/Anenii_Noi_District" title="Anenii Noi District">Anenii Noi</a>, and is thought to be the first winery in Bessarabia. It has since also become a tourist complex with a museum, art gallery, hotel, spa, and wine tasting rooms.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Agriculture">Agriculture</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Agriculture_in_Moldova" title="Agriculture in Moldova">Agriculture in Moldova</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Dniester_in_Moldova,_2004.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Dniester_in_Moldova%2C_2004.jpg/220px-Dniester_in_Moldova%2C_2004.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="181" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Dniester_in_Moldova%2C_2004.jpg/330px-Dniester_in_Moldova%2C_2004.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Dniester_in_Moldova%2C_2004.jpg/440px-Dniester_in_Moldova%2C_2004.jpg 2x" data-file-width="728" data-file-height="599" /></a><figcaption>Agricultural land in Dniester, 2004</figcaption></figure>
<p><a class="mw-selflink selflink">Moldova</a> is an agrarian-industrial state, with agricultural land occupying 2,499,000 hectares in a total area of 3,384,600 hectares.<sup id="cite_ref-:09_282-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:09-282">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup> It is estimated that 1,810,500 of these hectares are <a href="/wiki/Arable_land" title="Arable land">arable</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:09_282-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:09-282">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup> It is among the most arable countries in Europe, with the Chernozem soil across the <a href="/wiki/B%C4%83l%C8%9Bi_Steppe" title="Bălți Steppe">Bălți Steppe</a> being among the most fertile soils anywhere in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-283" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-283">&#91;278&#93;</a></sup> With more than 300 days of sunshine per year supporting the cultivation of vineyards, Moldova is also one of the largest wine producers in the world. Moldova's agricultural sector benefits from a geographical proximity to large markets, especially the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:09_282-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:09-282">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup> As of 2021, agriculture made up 12% of Moldova's overall exports and 21% of overall employment.<sup id="cite_ref-284" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-284">&#91;279&#93;</a></sup> Its most exported foods are maize, wheat, sunflower seeds, grapes, apples, sugar beets, milk, potatoes, barley, plums/sloes, while relevant and important domestic industries include sugar processing, vegetable oil, food processing, and agricultural machinery.<sup id="cite_ref-285" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-285">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup> Between 2015 and 2022, agricultural production has almost doubled, particularly in vegetable and fruit production.<sup id="cite_ref-286" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-286">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup> In July 2023, a network of 20 <a href="/wiki/Seed_library" title="Seed library">seed libraries</a> comprising over 1,000 seeds were created across Moldova with the assistance of <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Czech_Republic)" title="Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Czech Republic)">Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic</a>, <a href="/wiki/Non-governmental_organization" title="Non-governmental organization">NGO</a>s, and the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Development_Programme" title="United Nations Development Programme">United Nations Development Programme</a>, with the aim is to improve local <a href="/wiki/Agricultural_biodiversity" title="Agricultural biodiversity">agricultural biodiversity</a>, <a href="/wiki/Climate_resilience" title="Climate resilience">climate resilience</a>, and the capacity of local government and farmers to respond effectively to changing environmental conditions.<sup id="cite_ref-287" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-287">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Nevertheless, the country's agricultural sector faces serious long-term challenges. Despite having relatively modest per capita <a href="/wiki/Greenhouse_gas_emissions" title="Greenhouse gas emissions">greenhouse gas emissions</a>, and lower than the world average, Moldova is highly vulnerable to <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a> and related environmental disasters which already cost the country 2.13% of annual GDP.<sup id="cite_ref-288" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-288">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup> According to Climate-KIC, run by the <a href="/wiki/European_Institute_of_Innovation_and_Technology" title="European Institute of Innovation and Technology">European Institute of Innovation and Technology</a>, "The same region in Moldova can experience intense <a href="/wiki/Drought" title="Drought">droughts</a> and devastating <a href="/wiki/Flood" title="Flood">floods</a> in the course of a few months, which is the primary concern of local people when they talk about climate. But the irregular nature of these events made it difficult to sustain long term interest from Moldovan people or to channel money from donors."<sup id="cite_ref-289" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-289">&#91;284&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Transport_infrastructure">Transport infrastructure</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Transport_in_Moldova" title="Transport in Moldova">Transport in Moldova</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rail_transport_in_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="Rail transport in Moldova">Rail transport in Moldova</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Chisinau_Airport_KIV.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Chisinau_Airport_KIV.jpg/220px-Chisinau_Airport_KIV.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Chisinau_Airport_KIV.jpg/330px-Chisinau_Airport_KIV.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Chisinau_Airport_KIV.jpg/440px-Chisinau_Airport_KIV.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2576" data-file-height="1932" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u_International_Airport" title="Chișinău International Airport">Chișinău International Airport</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The main means of transportation in Moldova are railways 1,138&#160;km (707&#160;mi) and a highway system (12,730&#160;km or 7,910&#160;mi overall, including 10,937&#160;km or 6,796&#160;mi of paved surfaces). Rail links connect it via direct overnight trains to neighbouring <a href="/wiki/Bucharest" title="Bucharest">Bucharest</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kyiv" title="Kyiv">Kyiv</a>, <a href="/wiki/Odesa" title="Odesa">Odesa</a>, and also <a href="/wiki/Moscow" title="Moscow">Moscow</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_272-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-272">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Giurgiule%C8%99ti" title="Giurgiulești">Giurgiulești</a> terminal on the <a href="/wiki/Danube" title="Danube">Danube</a> is compatible with small seagoing vessels. Shipping on the lower <a href="/wiki/Prut" title="Prut">Prut</a> and <a href="/wiki/Nistru" class="mw-redirect" title="Nistru">Nistru</a> rivers plays only a modest role in the country's transportation system. 
</p><p>The sole international air gateway of Moldova is the <a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u_International_Airport" title="Chișinău International Airport">Chișinău International Airport</a>. with direct flights to and from many European destinations.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Telecommunications">Telecommunications</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Telecommunications_in_Moldova" title="Telecommunications in Moldova">Telecommunications in Moldova</a></div>
<p>Internet in Moldova is among of the fastest and least expensive in the world as of 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-290" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-290">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup> The country ranks 3rd in the world by gigabit coverage with around 90% of the population having the option to subscribe to a <a href="/wiki/Gigabit_Ethernet" title="Gigabit Ethernet">gigabit-speed</a> <a href="/wiki/Optical_fiber" title="Optical fiber">fibre-optic</a> broadband plan.<sup id="cite_ref-:010_291-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:010-291">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Development_Programme" title="United Nations Development Programme">United Nations Development Programme</a> has judged it to have a highly developed digital infrastructure, with 98% 4G coverage of its territory.<sup id="cite_ref-292" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-292">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> By July 2022, there were more than 3 million internet users in Moldova, constituting some 76% of the population.<sup id="cite_ref-293" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-293">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup> Moldova is considering a bid to begin rolling out 5G in 2024, with testing beginning in 2019. <a href="/wiki/Starlink" title="Starlink">Starlink</a> launched in Moldova in August 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Information_and_communications_technology" title="Information and communications technology">Information and Communication Technology</a> (ICT) is one of the most promising economic sectors in Moldova, accounting for more than 10 percent of GDP. More than 2,000 Moldovan students per year graduate with a degree in <a href="/wiki/Bachelor_of_Computing" title="Bachelor of Computing">computing</a> or a related field.<sup id="cite_ref-:010_291-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:010-291">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/International_Telecommunication_Union" title="International Telecommunication Union">ITU</a>'s Global Cybersecurity Index ranks Moldova on the 33rd place in Europe and the 63rd place in the world. The country's joining in 2009 of the <a href="/wiki/Convention_on_Cybercrime" title="Convention on Cybercrime">Convention on Cybercrime</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a> and adoption of the National Cyber Security Program for 2016–2020 have established the legislative parameters for a safer digital environment. Since Russia's invasion of neighbouring Ukraine and their campaign of <a href="/wiki/Cyberwarfare_by_Russia" title="Cyberwarfare by Russia">cyberwarfare</a> against Moldova, the Moldovan government has invested significant money and resources in developing stronger <a href="/wiki/Cybersecurity" class="mw-redirect" title="Cybersecurity">cybersecurity</a> practices and regulations with assistance from the European Union and United States.<sup id="cite_ref-295" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup> The European Union has also set up and funded the Moldova Cybersecurity Rapid Assistance Unit to improve the cyber resilience of Moldova's public sector organisations and key critical infrastructure sectors. Moldova has adopted new legislation partially drafted by the unit which will go into effect on 1 January 2025.<sup id="cite_ref-297" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-297">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup> The country has also passed legislation in order to more closely align with the EU's <a href="/wiki/General_Data_Protection_Regulation" title="General Data Protection Regulation">GDPR</a> regulations, and is currently mostly compliant.<sup id="cite_ref-299" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-299">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Demographics">Demographics</span></h2>
<p>The most up-to-date and reliable information is available from the <a href="/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Statistics_of_the_Republic_of_Moldova" title="National Bureau of Statistics of the Republic of Moldova">National Bureau of Statistics of the Republic of Moldova</a>'s website which is continuously updated on a monthly and yearly basis. The most recent <a href="/wiki/National_Census" class="mw-redirect" title="National Census">national census</a> of Moldova was carried out in <a href="/wiki/2014_Moldovan_census" title="2014 Moldovan census">2014</a> (not including <a href="/wiki/Transnistria" title="Transnistria">Transnistria</a>). The next national census is due to be carried out in 2024.<sup id="cite_ref-300" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-300">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<div class="thumbcaption">
<p>Population of Moldova according to ethnic group
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r981673959">.mw-parser-output .legend{page-break-inside:avoid;break-inside:avoid-column}.mw-parser-output .legend-color{display:inline-block;min-width:1.25em;height:1.25em;line-height:1.25;margin:1px 0;text-align:center;border:1px solid black;background-color:transparent;color:black}.mw-parser-output .legend-text{}</style><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#1F78B4; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Moldovans" title="Moldovans">Moldovans</a> (75%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#33A02C; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Romanians" title="Romanians">Romanians</a> (7%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#E31A1C; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Ukrainians" title="Ukrainians">Ukrainians</a> (6.57%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#FF7F00; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Gagauzians" class="mw-redirect" title="Gagauzians">Gagauzians</a> (4.57%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#6A3D9A; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Russians" title="Russians">Russians</a> (4.06%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#B15928; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Bulgarians" title="Bulgarians">Bulgarians</a> (1.88%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#A6CEE3; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Romani_people" title="Romani people">Romani</a> (0.34%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#B2DF8A; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Belarusians" title="Belarusians">Belarusians</a> (0.10%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#FB9A99; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Jews" title="Jews">Jews</a> (0.06%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#FDBF6F; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Poles_(people)" class="mw-redirect" title="Poles (people)">Poles</a> (0.05%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#CAB2D6; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Germans" title="Germans">Germans</a> (0.03%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#FFFF99; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;Others (0.26%)</div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0">Source: <a href="/wiki/2014_Moldovan_census" title="2014 Moldovan census">2014 Moldovan census</a>.</p>
</div>
</div></div><p>Moldova has an estimated population of approx. 2,512,800 people as of 1 January 2023, about 52,300 lower than at the start of 2022, making Moldova among the least populous nations in <a href="/wiki/Europe" title="Europe">Europe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> Moldova is relatively <a href="/wiki/Urbanization" title="Urbanization">urbanised</a>, with 43.4% of Moldovans living in urban areas as of 2022 and an urbanisation rate of 0.09%.<sup id="cite_ref-302" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-302">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup> About one-third of the Moldovan population live in the capital city <a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Chișinău">Chișinău</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Metropolis_of_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u_and_All_Moldova" title="Metropolis of Chișinău and All Moldova">metropolitan area</a>. As of 2022, the country's <a href="/wiki/Population_density" title="Population density">population density</a> is 82.8 inhabitants per 1 km<sup>2</sup>, and average life expectancy was 71.5 years (67.2 for males, and 75.7 for females).<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> There are 100 women per 90 men in Moldova, and employed women have significantly higher levels of education, though women continued to earn 13.6% less than men on average.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> The number of elderly people (60 years and over) per 100 inhabitants in Moldova has increased year-on-year.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> The national language is <a href="/wiki/Romanian_language" title="Romanian language">Romanian</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Romance_languages" title="Romance languages">Romance language</a>, though approximately 15% of the Moldovan population also speak <a href="/wiki/Russian_language" title="Russian language">Russian</a> as of 2014.
</p><p>The country has been suffering from long-term population decline due to high levels of <a href="/wiki/Emigration_from_Moldova" title="Emigration from Moldova">emigration</a> (in 2022, 43,000 more people left the country than came) as well as low fertility rates. According to <a href="/wiki/Balkan_Insight" title="Balkan Insight">Balkan Insight</a>, the population has fallen by almost 33% since 1990, and by 2035 the total population may be half what it was in 1990.<sup id="cite_ref-304" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-304">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup> Since 2018, the number of deaths has exceeded the levels of live-births, though the gap has been reduced since 2021. As of 2022, the average number of children per women of childbearing age was 1.69, well below the <a href="/wiki/Replacement_rate" class="mw-redirect" title="Replacement rate">replacement rate</a> of 2.1, as compared to 1.78 in 2019. The total number of deaths fell by 20.5% in 2022 compared to 2019. Unemployment has remained low at about 3% in 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to the <a href="/wiki/2014_Moldovan_census" title="2014 Moldovan census">2014 national census</a>, ethnic <a href="/wiki/Moldovans" title="Moldovans">Moldovans</a> made up approx. 75% of the country's population, while <a href="/wiki/Romanians" title="Romanians">Romanians</a> (7%), <a href="/wiki/Ukrainians" title="Ukrainians">Ukrainians</a> (6.57%), <a href="/wiki/Gagauz_people" title="Gagauz people">Gagauzians</a> (4.57%), and <a href="/wiki/Russians" title="Russians">Russians</a> (4.06%) made up the most substantial ethnic minorities. Smaller populations include <a href="/wiki/Bulgarians" title="Bulgarians">Bulgarians</a> (1.88%), <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romani</a> (0.34%), <a href="/wiki/Belarusians" title="Belarusians">Belarusians</a> (0.10%), <a href="/wiki/Jews" title="Jews">Jews</a> (0.06%), and <a href="/wiki/Polish_people" title="Polish people">Poles</a> (0.05%).
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Language">Language</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Languages_of_Moldova" title="Languages of Moldova">Languages of Moldova</a></div>
<p>As of March 2023, the only <a href="/wiki/Official_language" title="Official language">official language</a> of Moldova is Romanian, and all references to the Moldovan language in the <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Moldova" title="Constitution of Moldova">constitution</a> and legal bills have been amended to refer to Romanian.<sup id="cite_ref-305" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-305">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-306" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-306">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup> The 2014 Moldovan census for the first time collected information about the languages spoken by residents in Moldova. It is worth noting that there is a <a href="/wiki/Controversy_over_ethnic_and_linguistic_identity_in_Moldova" title="Controversy over ethnic and linguistic identity in Moldova">controversy</a> about whether or not <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_language" title="Moldovan language">Moldovan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Romanian_language" title="Romanian language">Romanian</a> should be considered distinct languages, and the Moldovan government rejects any distinction, however the census allowed for respondents to respond with their preferred label. The results were <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_language" title="Moldovan language">Moldovan</a> (54.6%), <a href="/wiki/Romanian_language" title="Romanian language">Romanian</a> (24.0%), <a href="/wiki/Russian_language" title="Russian language">Russian</a> (14.5%), <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_language" title="Ukrainian language">Ukrainian</a> (2.7%), <a href="/wiki/Gagauz_language" title="Gagauz language">Gagauz</a> (2.7%), <a href="/wiki/Bulgarian_language" title="Bulgarian language">Bulgarian</a> (1.7%), and Other (0.5%).
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Diaspora_and_emigration">Diaspora and emigration</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_diaspora" title="Moldovan diaspora">Moldovan diaspora</a></div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Emigration_from_Moldova" title="Emigration from Moldova">Emigration from Moldova</a></div>
<p>Emigration is a mass phenomenon in Moldova and has a major impact on the country's <a href="/wiki/Demographics" class="mw-redirect" title="Demographics">demographics</a> and economy. It is estimated that more than between 1.2 and 2 million Moldovan citizens (over 25% of the population) are living and working abroad.<sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup> The Moldovan economy is still heavily reliant on their remittance payments. Moldovans are found across the <a href="/wiki/Balkans" title="Balkans">Balkan</a> region, <a href="/wiki/Western_Europe" title="Western Europe">Western Europe</a>, and <a href="/wiki/North_America" title="North America">North America</a>. Among the most notable Moldovan <a href="/wiki/Diaspora" title="Diaspora">diaspora</a> populations are: 285,000 in <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a> (2020), 258,600 in <a href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</a> (2002) 156,400 in <a href="/wiki/Russia" title="Russia">Russia</a> (2010), 188,923 in <a href="/wiki/Italy" title="Italy">Italy</a> (2019), 122,000 in <a href="/wiki/Germany" title="Germany">Germany</a> (2022), 26,300 in <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a> (2019), and 20,470 in <a href="/wiki/Canada" title="Canada">Canada</a> (2021).
</p><p>Current trends indicate that the population of Moldova will continue to fall with emigration remaining both chronic and higher than immigration or natural birth rates. In 2020, net emigration fell to a low of 7,000, but by 2022, 43,000 more people left the country than came, though this is slightly down from net emigration of 45,000 in 2021. <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russia's invasion</a> of neighbouring Ukraine and the economic impact on Moldova may have been a key contributing factor in the rise from 2020 to 2022. However, there are indications that the invasion of Ukraine and the country's moves towards <a href="/wiki/Accession_of_Moldova_to_the_European_Union" title="Accession of Moldova to the European Union">accession to the European Union</a> may have led to a rise in the number of Moldovan emigrants returning to their country of birth, seeking to help the country join the EU.<sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> The Moldovan diaspora has also had a signifiant influent in recent Moldovan elections, voting overwhelmingly for <a href="/wiki/Maia_Sandu" title="Maia Sandu">Maia Sandu</a> as President in <a href="/wiki/2020_Moldovan_presidential_election" title="2020 Moldovan presidential election">2020</a> and for her <a href="/wiki/Party_of_Action_and_Solidarity" title="Party of Action and Solidarity">Party of Action and Solidarity</a> in the <a href="/wiki/2021_Moldovan_parliamentary_election" title="2021 Moldovan parliamentary election">2021 parliamentary election</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Religion">Religion</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Religion_in_Moldova" title="Religion in Moldova">Religion in Moldova</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Nativity_Cathedral_-_Moldova_(by_David_Stanley).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Nativity_Cathedral_-_Moldova_%28by_David_Stanley%29.jpg/220px-Nativity_Cathedral_-_Moldova_%28by_David_Stanley%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Nativity_Cathedral_-_Moldova_%28by_David_Stanley%29.jpg/330px-Nativity_Cathedral_-_Moldova_%28by_David_Stanley%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Nativity_Cathedral_-_Moldova_%28by_David_Stanley%29.jpg/440px-Nativity_Cathedral_-_Moldova_%28by_David_Stanley%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="768" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Nativity_Cathedral,_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Nativity Cathedral, Chișinău">Nativity Cathedral, Chişinău</a>. <a href="/wiki/Metropolis_of_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u_and_All_Moldova" title="Metropolis of Chișinău and All Moldova">Moldovan Orthodox Church</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Moldova's constitution provides for freedom of religion and complete separation of church and state, though the constitution cites the "exceptional importance" of <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Christianity" class="mw-redirect" title="Eastern Orthodox Christianity">Eastern Orthodox Christianity</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_311-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-311">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Religious_discrimination" title="Religious discrimination">Discrimination</a> on the basis of religious affiliation is illegal, and <a href="/wiki/Hate_speech" title="Hate speech">incitement to religious and ethnic hatred</a> was made illegal in May 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_311-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-311">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> Religion in Moldova is dominated by the <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church" title="Eastern Orthodox Church">Eastern Orthodox</a> branch of <a href="/wiki/Christianity" title="Christianity">Christianity</a>. According to the 2014 Moldovan census, 90% of the country reported to be of the Eastern Orthodox Christian faith.<sup id="cite_ref-312" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-312">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> Of this number, approx. 80–90% of Orthodox Moldovans belong to the Moldovan Orthodox Church (formally known as <a href="/wiki/Metropolis_of_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u_and_All_Moldova" title="Metropolis of Chișinău and All Moldova">Metropolis of Chișinău and All Moldova</a>) which is subordinate to the <a href="/wiki/Russian_Orthodox_Church" title="Russian Orthodox Church">Russian Orthodox Church</a>, and has played a powerful role in deepening Russia's influence in Moldova.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_311-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-311">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-313" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-313">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup> The remaining 10–20% of Orthodox Moldovans belong to the <a href="/wiki/Metropolis_of_Bessarabia" title="Metropolis of Bessarabia">Metropolis of Bessarabia</a>, which is subordinate to the <a href="/wiki/Romanian_Orthodox_Church" title="Romanian Orthodox Church">Romanian Orthodox Church</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_311-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-311">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Of the non-Orthodox population of Moldova, the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State" title="United States Department of State">United States Department of State</a> estimates that as of 2022 approx. 7% identify with no religion; <a href="/wiki/Baptists" title="Baptists">Baptists</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jehovah%27s_Witnesses" title="Jehovah&#39;s Witnesses">Jehovah's Witnesses</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Pentecostalism" title="Pentecostalism">Pentecostals</a> number between 15,000 and 30,000 each; the <a href="/wiki/Jewish_Community_of_the_Republic_of_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish Community of the Republic of Moldova">Jewish Community of the Republic of Moldova</a> organisation estimates the <a href="/wiki/Judaism" title="Judaism">Jewish</a> population to be approx. 20,000; and the Islamic League of Moldova (an <a href="/wiki/Non-governmental_organization" title="Non-governmental organization">NGO</a> recognised by the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Justice_(Moldova)" title="Ministry of Justice (Moldova)">Moldovan Ministry of Justice</a> in 2011 as representing <a href="/wiki/Islam_in_Moldova" title="Islam in Moldova">Moldovan Muslims</a><sup id="cite_ref-314" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-314">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup>) estimates the number of Muslims to be approx. 15,000–17,000.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_311-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-311">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> There are six <a href="/wiki/List_of_synagogues_in_Moldova" title="List of synagogues in Moldova">synagogues</a> in <a href="/wiki/Metropolis_of_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u_and_All_Moldova" title="Metropolis of Chișinău and All Moldova">Chișinău</a>, one in <a href="/wiki/Orhei" title="Orhei">Orhei</a>, one in <a href="/wiki/Soroca" title="Soroca">Soroca</a>, and one in <a href="/wiki/Tiraspol" title="Tiraspol">Tiraspol</a>, and one mosque in <a href="/wiki/Metropolis_of_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u_and_All_Moldova" title="Metropolis of Chișinău and All Moldova">Chișinău</a>. The remaining less than 5% of the Moldovan population are <a href="/wiki/Seventh-day_Adventist_Church" title="Seventh-day Adventist Church">Seventh-day Adventists</a>, <a href="/wiki/Evangelicalism" title="Evangelicalism">Evangelical Christians</a>, <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church" title="Catholic Church">Roman Catholics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lutheranism" title="Lutheranism">Lutherans</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Atheism" title="Atheism">atheists</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_311-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-311">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Transnistria" title="Government of Transnistria">Transnistrian authorities</a> estimate that 80% of the population belong to the Moldovan Orthodox Church.<sup id="cite_ref-:14_311-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-311">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Health_and_fertility">Health and fertility</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Health_in_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="Health in Moldova">Health in Moldova</a> and <a href="/wiki/Healthcare_in_Moldova" title="Healthcare in Moldova">Healthcare in Moldova</a></div><div class="PieChartTemplate thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:202px">
<div class="mw-no-invert" style="background-color:white;margin:auto;position:relative;width:200px;height:200px;overflow:hidden;border-radius:100px;border:1px solid black;transform:scaleX(-1)rotate(-90deg)">
<div style="border:solid transparent;background-color: initial;position:absolute;width:100px;line-height:0;left:0; top:0; border-width:0 200px 200px 0; border-color:#6A3D9A"></div><div style="border:solid transparent;background-color: initial;position:absolute;width:100px;line-height:0;left:100px; top:100px; border-width:100px 0 0 321.4582078634px; border-left-color:#FF7F00"></div>
<div style="position:absolute;line-height:0;border-style:solid;left:0;top:0;border-width:0 200px 100px 0;border-color:#FF7F00"></div>
<div style="position:absolute;line-height:0;border-style:solid;left:0;top:0;border-width:0 100px 200px 0;border-color:#FF7F00"></div><div style="border:solid transparent;background-color: initial;position:absolute;width:100px;line-height:0;left:100px; top:100px; border-width:100px 0 0 102.54539447886px; border-left-color:#E31A1C"></div>
<div style="position:absolute;line-height:0;border-style:solid;left:0;top:0;border-width:0 200px 100px 0;border-color:#E31A1C"></div>

<div style="position:absolute;line-height:0;border-style:solid;left:0;top:0;border-width:0 200px 100px 0;border-color:#33A02C"></div><div style="border:solid transparent;background-color: initial;position:absolute;width:100px;line-height:0;right:100px; top:100px; border-width:48.175367410172px 87.630668004386px 0 0; border-top-color:#1F78B4"></div>
<div style="position:absolute;line-height:0;border-style:solid;left:0;top:0;border-width:0 200px 100px 0;border-color:#1F78B4"></div>
</div>
<div class="thumbcaption">
<p>Structure of deaths by major classes of causes of death in 2022
</p>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#1F78B4; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Cardiovascular_disease" title="Cardiovascular disease">Diseases of the circulatory system</a> (58%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#33A02C; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Cancer" title="Cancer">Cancerous tumours</a> (15.8%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#E31A1C; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;Other causes (13.9%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#FF7F00; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Gastrointestinal_disease" title="Gastrointestinal disease">Diseases of the digestive tract</a> (7.5%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:#6A3D9A; color:;">&#160;</span>&#160;External causes (4.8%)</div>
</div>
</div></div><p>Moldova provides <a href="/wiki/Universal_health_care" title="Universal health care">universal healthcare</a> through a <a href="/wiki/Mandatory_health_insurance" class="mw-redirect" title="Mandatory health insurance">mandatory health insurance</a> scheme. According to the most recent 2022 official data, per 10,000 inhabitants there are 48.4 doctors and 91 units of average medical staff.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> Approx. 53% of those aged 16 and over in urban areas described their own health as 'good' or 'very good', compared to approx. 33% of people of the same age in rural areas.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> The country has 86 <a href="/wiki/Hospital" title="Hospital">hospitals</a>, 1,524 <a href="/wiki/Pharmacy_(shop)" title="Pharmacy (shop)">pharmacies</a> and branches, 12,600 <a href="/wiki/Physician" title="Physician">physicians</a>, 23,687 <a href="/wiki/Paramedic" title="Paramedic">paramedical</a> personnel, and 17,293 <a href="/wiki/Hospital_bed" title="Hospital bed">hospital beds</a>. Moldova spends 6% of its annual GDP on health care, up from 4.9% in 2019.
</p><p>As of 2022, the average life expectancy was 71.5 years (67.2 for males, and 75.7 for females), slightly lower than comparable countries such as <a href="/wiki/Albania" title="Albania">Albania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bulgaria" title="Bulgaria">Bulgaria</a>, <a href="/wiki/Latvia" title="Latvia">Latvia</a>, and Ukraine. The number of elderly people (aged 60 years and over) per 100 inhabitants in Moldova has increased year-on-year. The <a href="/wiki/Total_fertility_rate" title="Total fertility rate">total fertility rate</a> per woman in 2022 was 1.69, a fall from 1.78 in 2019, and below the replacement rate of 2.1. There were 10.6 <a href="/wiki/Live_birth_rate" class="mw-redirect" title="Live birth rate">live births</a> per 1,000 inhabitants in 2022, a drop from 12.2 in 2019, and 14.2 deaths per 1,000 inhabitants, an increase from 13.7 in 2019 but a significant fall from 17.5 in 2019. <a href="/wiki/Infant_mortality" title="Infant mortality">Infant mortality</a> per 1,000 live-births was 9.0, a slight increase on 8.7 in 2020.
</p><p>The overall number of deaths fell by 20.5% compared to 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> According to the National Agency for Public Health, the major causes of death in 2022 were <a href="/wiki/Cardiovascular_disease" title="Cardiovascular disease">diseases of the circulatory system</a> (58%), <a href="/wiki/Cancerous_tumour" class="mw-redirect" title="Cancerous tumour">cancerous tumours</a> (15.8%), <a href="/wiki/Gastrointestinal_disease" title="Gastrointestinal disease">diseases of the digestive tract</a> (7.5%), external causes (4.8%), and other causes (13.9%).<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> More specifically, the leading causes of death in 2019 were <a href="/wiki/Coronary_artery_disease" title="Coronary artery disease">Ischaemic heart disease</a>, <a href="/wiki/Stroke" title="Stroke">strokes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hypertensive_heart_disease" title="Hypertensive heart disease">hypertensive heart disease</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cirrhosis" title="Cirrhosis">cirrhosis</a> of the liver, and trachea, bronchus, and <a href="/wiki/Lung_cancer" title="Lung cancer">lung cancers</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:042_315-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:042-315">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 19 December 2016, the Moldovan parliament approved raising the retirement age to 63 years<sup id="cite_ref-316" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-316">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup> from the current level of 57 for women and 62 for men, a reform that is part of a 3-year-old assistance program agreed with the <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">International Monetary Fund</a>. The retirement age will be lifted gradually by a few months every year until it is fully in effect in 2028.<sup id="cite_ref-317" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-317">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Education">Education</span></h3>
<p>As of the academic year 2022/23, Moldova had 1,218 <a href="/wiki/Primary_school" title="Primary school">primary</a> and <a href="/wiki/Secondary_school" title="Secondary school">secondary</a> schools, 90 <a href="/wiki/Vocational_school" title="Vocational school">vocational schools</a>, and 21 <a href="/wiki/Higher_education" title="Higher education">higher education</a> institutions, as well as 12 <a href="/wiki/Private_university" title="Private university">private</a> higher education institutions.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-318" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-318">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup> There were a total of 437,000 pupils and students. As of 2015<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Moldova&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a> allocates 5,000 scholarships in high schools and universities for Moldovan students.<sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup> Likewise, more than half of preschool children in Moldova benefit from Romania funded program to renovate and equip <a href="/wiki/Kindergarten" title="Kindergarten">kindergartens</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup> Almost all the population is literate: the <a href="/wiki/Literacy_rate" class="mw-redirect" title="Literacy rate">literacy rate</a> of the population aged 15 and over is estimated at 99.6%.<sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:State_University_of_Moldova_main_building_entrance.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/State_University_of_Moldova_main_building_entrance.jpg/220px-State_University_of_Moldova_main_building_entrance.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/State_University_of_Moldova_main_building_entrance.jpg/330px-State_University_of_Moldova_main_building_entrance.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/State_University_of_Moldova_main_building_entrance.jpg/440px-State_University_of_Moldova_main_building_entrance.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4128" data-file-height="3096" /></a><figcaption>Main building entrance of the <a href="/wiki/Moldova_State_University" title="Moldova State University">Moldova State University</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The main higher education institutions in Moldova are the <a href="/wiki/Moldova_State_University" title="Moldova State University">Moldova State University</a> (est. 1946) and the <a href="/wiki/Academy_of_Sciences_of_Moldova" title="Academy of Sciences of Moldova">Academy of Sciences of Moldova</a> (est. 1961), both of which are located in <a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Chișinău">Chișinău</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Academy_of_Economic_Studies_of_Moldova" title="Academy of Economic Studies of Moldova">Academy of Economic Studies of Moldova</a> (est. 1991) has featured on the <a href="/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings" title="Times Higher Education World University Rankings">Times Higher Education World University Rankings</a> and has educated a number of national leaders including current <a href="/wiki/President_of_Moldova" title="President of Moldova">President of Moldova</a> <a href="/wiki/Maia_Sandu" title="Maia Sandu">Maia Sandu</a> and leader of the opposition <a href="/wiki/Igor_Dodon" title="Igor Dodon">Igor Dodon</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup> Other important universities include the <a href="/wiki/Ion_Creang%C4%83_State_Pedagogical_University_of_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Ion Creangă State Pedagogical University of Chișinău">Ion Creangă State Pedagogical University of Chișinău</a> (est. 1940), <a href="/wiki/Nicolae_Testemi%C8%9Banu_State_University_of_Medicine_and_Pharmacy" title="Nicolae Testemițanu State University of Medicine and Pharmacy">Nicolae Testemițanu State University of Medicine and Pharmacy</a> (est. 1945), and the <a href="/wiki/Technical_University_of_Moldova" title="Technical University of Moldova">Technical University of Moldova</a> (est. 1964). Women account for 59.1% of students in higher education, and 70.1% of all foreign students in <a href="/wiki/Postgraduate_education" title="Postgraduate education">doctoral programmes</a> in Moldova. 32.3% of employed women in Moldova have received higher education, compared to 24.5% of men, and 16.9% specialised secondary education compared to 11.3% of men.<sup id="cite_ref-:013_301-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:013-301">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Regional_differences_and_tensions">Regional differences and tensions</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Transnistria_conflict" title="Transnistria conflict">Transnistria conflict</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gagauzia" title="Gagauzia">Gagauzia</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Unification_of_Moldova_and_Romania" title="Unification of Moldova and Romania">Unification of Moldova and Romania</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Transnistria_Tank_Bender.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Transnistria_Tank_Bender.JPG/220px-Transnistria_Tank_Bender.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Transnistria_Tank_Bender.JPG/330px-Transnistria_Tank_Bender.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Transnistria_Tank_Bender.JPG/440px-Transnistria_Tank_Bender.JPG 2x" data-file-width="2700" data-file-height="1800" /></a><figcaption>Tank in <a href="/wiki/Bender,_Moldova" title="Bender, Moldova">Bender</a>, Moldova</figcaption></figure>
<p>Since independence, Moldova characterised by a substantial range of profound regional differences across its internationally recognised territory. Since <a href="/wiki/Independence_Day_of_the_Republic_of_Moldova" title="Independence Day of the Republic of Moldova">independence</a>, the country has struggled with issues of national identity, geopolitical strategy, and alliances, often torn between <a href="/wiki/Romania" title="Romania">Romania</a> and the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> to the west and the <a href="/wiki/Russian_federation" class="mw-redirect" title="Russian federation">Russian Federation</a> to the east. Most notably, in eastern Moldova is the unrecognised breakaway state of <a href="/wiki/Transnistria" title="Transnistria">Transnistria</a>, which lies on the eastern bank of the <a href="/wiki/Dniester" title="Dniester">Dniester</a> river and borders <a href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</a>, which has pursued close diplomatic, military, and economic ties with Russia <a href="/wiki/Transnistria_War" title="Transnistria War">since 1992</a>, with more than a thousand Russian soldiers stationed in the region. This has proved particularly difficult following <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russia's invasion of Ukraine</a> in 2022, as Transnistria's position on Ukraine's south-western flank and its hosting of more than a thousand Russian soldiers poses a potential threat to Ukraine's war efforts. The European Union's <a href="/wiki/High_Representative_of_the_Union_for_Foreign_Affairs_and_Security_Policy" title="High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy">High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy</a> <a href="/wiki/Josep_Borrell" title="Josep Borrell">Josep Borrell</a> has confirmed that the pathway to accession does not depend upon a resolution of the <a href="/wiki/Transnistria_conflict" title="Transnistria conflict">Transnistria conflict</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Gagauz.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Gagauz.jpg/220px-Gagauz.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Gagauz.jpg/330px-Gagauz.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Gagauz.jpg/440px-Gagauz.jpg 2x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="428" /></a><figcaption>Gagauzian people</figcaption></figure>
<p>There is further the issue of the <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_territorial_unit" title="Autonomous territorial unit">autonomous territorial unit</a> of <a href="/wiki/Gagauzia" title="Gagauzia">Gagauzia</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Gagauz_people" title="Gagauz people">Gagauz people</a> are a <a href="/wiki/Turkic_languages" title="Turkic languages">Turkic-speaking</a> people spread between southern Moldova and the south-west of Ukraine. While their exact origin is considered obscure, they have a strong sense of ethnic identity distinct from that of Moldova, Romania, and Ukraine, with a <a href="/wiki/Gagauz_language" title="Gagauz language">distinctive language</a> and cultural traditions. They are nevertheless a heavily <a href="/wiki/Russification" title="Russification">Russified</a> group.<sup id="cite_ref-:7_324-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-324">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup> Support for integration with Romania and the European Union is substantially lower among Gagauzians than among the broader Moldovan population. In 2014, shortly before the Republic of Moldova signed its EU Association Agreement, nearly 99 per cent of Gagauzians voted in a referendum "to reject closer links with Europe in favour of joining the Russian-led Eurasian Economic Union."<sup id="cite_ref-:22_325-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:22-325">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> In 2015, "just over half of Gagauzians voted for the Russian-backed socialist candidate <a href="/wiki/Irina_Vlah" title="Irina Vlah">Irina Vlakh</a> as governor."<sup id="cite_ref-:22_325-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:22-325">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> Gagauzia continues to represent a serious challenge both to Moldova's territorial sovereignty and political stability due to Russia's systemic involvement in the region, especially by backing pro-Russian local parties and leadership candidates.<sup id="cite_ref-:7_324-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-324">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/European_Centre_for_Minority_Issues" title="European Centre for Minority Issues">European Centre for Minority Issues</a> has also highlighted the role of supposedly-neutral NGO groups in Gagauzia as a new front in Russia's <a href="/wiki/Hybrid_warfare" title="Hybrid warfare">hybrid-war</a> against both Moldova and Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-:7_324-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-324">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup> The region's current local leader, <a href="/wiki/Evghenia_Gu%C8%9Bul" title="Evghenia Guțul">Evghenia Guțul</a>, in July 2023 thanked the fugitive Moldovan <a href="/wiki/Oligarchy" title="Oligarchy">oligarch</a> <a href="/wiki/Ilan_Shor" title="Ilan Shor">Ilan Shor</a>, leader of the outlawed Moldovan pro-Russian opposition <a href="/wiki/%C8%98or_Party" title="Șor Party">Șor Party</a>, for his personal and financial support and his "willingness to do what it takes so that we may fulfil our election promises", and expressed a desire for deeper diplomatic ties with Russia.<sup id="cite_ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>There is also <a href="/wiki/Controversy_over_ethnic_and_linguistic_identity_in_Moldova" title="Controversy over ethnic and linguistic identity in Moldova">substantial controversy</a> over ethnic and linguistic identity in Moldova concerning whether the <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_language" title="Moldovan language">Moldovan language</a> and <a href="/wiki/Moldovans" title="Moldovans">Moldovan people</a> constitute separate linguistic and ethnic groups to the <a href="/wiki/Romanian_language" title="Romanian language">Romanian language</a> and <a href="/wiki/Romanians" title="Romanians">Romanian people</a>. The possibility of the <a href="/wiki/Unification_of_Moldova_and_Romania" title="Unification of Moldova and Romania">unification of Moldova and Romania</a> has remained a popular topic in both countries since Moldova's independence in 1991. Romania and Moldova enjoy exceptionally strong <a href="/wiki/Moldova%E2%80%93Romania_relations" title="Moldova–Romania relations">diplomatic relations</a>. Romania supports Moldova's rapid accession to the European Union, provides vast economic assistance to Moldova's struggling economy, and provided up to 90% of Moldova's energy needs via discounted capped prices as Moldova sought to reduce its reliance on Russian oil and natural gas.<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> Relations have strengthened further since Russia's invasion of Ukraine.<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup> Up to 74% of the Romanian public and more than 40% of the Moldovan public would support Moldova being integrated into Romania in one form or another, though most in either country believe that 'now is not the right time'.<sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup> A 2022 survey during the <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russian invasion of Ukraine</a> indicated that only 11% of Romania's population supports an immediate union, while over 42% think it is not the moment.<sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Culture">Culture</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Moldova" title="Culture of Moldova">Culture of Moldova</a></div>
