2x" data-file-width="3099" data-file-height="4448" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Dimitrie_Cantemir" title="Dimitrie Cantemir">Dimitrie Cantemir</a>, Moldavian scholar of the early Enlightenment</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Moldova's cultural tradition has been influenced primarily by the <a href="/wiki/Origin_of_the_Romanians" title="Origin of the Romanians">Romanian origins</a> of its majority population, the roots of which go back to the second century AD, the period of <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Rome" title="Ancient Rome">Roman</a> colonization in <a href="/wiki/Dacia" title="Dacia">Dacia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-culture_333-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-culture-333">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup> Located geographically at the crossroads of <a href="/wiki/Italic_peoples" title="Italic peoples">Latin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Slavic_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Slavic people">Slavic</a> and other cultures, Moldova has enriched its own culture adopting and maintaining traditions of neighbouring regions and of other influential sources.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup> The largest ethnic group, which had come to identify itself widely as "Moldovan" by the 14th century, played a significant role in the shaping of <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Romania#Classical_age" title="Culture of Romania">classical Romanian culture</a>. The culture has been also influenced by the <a href="/wiki/Byzantine" class="mw-redirect" title="Byzantine">Byzantine</a> culture, the neighbouring Magyar and Slavic populations, and later by the Ottoman Turks. A strong Western European influence in Moldovan literature and arts was prevalent in the 19th century. During the periods 1812–1917 and 1944–89, Moldovans were influenced by Russian and Soviet administrative control as well and by ethnic Russian immigration.<sup id="cite_ref-culture_333-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-culture-333">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:International_Children%27s_Day_Celebrations_in_Chisinau,_Moldova_(7688594362_cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/International_Children%27s_Day_Celebrations_in_Chisinau%2C_Moldova_%287688594362_cropped%29.jpg/220px-International_Children%27s_Day_Celebrations_in_Chisinau%2C_Moldova_%287688594362_cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/International_Children%27s_Day_Celebrations_in_Chisinau%2C_Moldova_%287688594362_cropped%29.jpg/330px-International_Children%27s_Day_Celebrations_in_Chisinau%2C_Moldova_%287688594362_cropped%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/International_Children%27s_Day_Celebrations_in_Chisinau%2C_Moldova_%287688594362_cropped%29.jpg/440px-International_Children%27s_Day_Celebrations_in_Chisinau%2C_Moldova_%287688594362_cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1313" data-file-height="877" /></a><figcaption>Moldovans wearing <a href="/wiki/Romanian_dress" title="Romanian dress">national costumes</a> in <a href="/wiki/Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="Chișinău">Chișinău</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The country's cultural heritage was marked by numerous churches and monasteries built by the Moldavian ruler <a href="/wiki/Stephen_the_Great" title="Stephen the Great">Stephen the Great</a> in the 15th century, by the works of the later renaissance Metropolitans <a href="/wiki/Varlaam,_Metropolitan_of_Moscow" title="Varlaam, Metropolitan of Moscow">Varlaam</a> and <a href="/wiki/Dosoftei" title="Dosoftei">Dosoftei</a>, and those of scholars such as <a href="/wiki/Grigore_Ureche" title="Grigore Ureche">Grigore Ureche</a>, <a href="/wiki/Miron_Costin" title="Miron Costin">Miron Costin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nicolae_Milescu" class="mw-redirect" title="Nicolae Milescu">Nicolae Milescu</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dimitrie_Cantemir" title="Dimitrie Cantemir">Dimitrie Cantemir</a><sup id="cite_ref-fn6_335-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fn6-335">&#91;f&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Ion_Neculce" title="Ion Neculce">Ion Neculce</a>. In the 19th century, Moldavians from the territories of the medieval Principality of <a href="/wiki/Moldavia" title="Moldavia">Moldavia</a>, divided into <a href="/wiki/Bessarabia" title="Bessarabia">Bessarabia</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bukovina" title="Bukovina">Bukovina</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Western_Moldavia" title="Western Moldavia">Western Moldavia</a> (after 1859, Romania), made a significant contribution to the formation of the modern Romanian culture. Among these were many Bessarabians, such as <a href="/wiki/Alecu_Donici" title="Alecu Donici">Alexandru Donici</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alexandru_H%C3%A2jdeu" title="Alexandru Hâjdeu">Alexandru Hâjdeu</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bogdan_Petriceicu_Hasdeu" title="Bogdan Petriceicu Hasdeu">Bogdan Petriceicu Hasdeu</a>, <a href="/wiki/Constantin_Stamati" title="Constantin Stamati">Constantin Stamati</a>, <a href="/wiki/Constantin_Stamati-Ciurea" title="Constantin Stamati-Ciurea">Constantin Stamati-Ciurea</a>, <a href="/wiki/Costache_Negruzzi" class="mw-redirect" title="Costache Negruzzi">Costache Negruzzi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alecu_Russo" title="Alecu Russo">Alecu Russo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Constantin_Stere" title="Constantin Stere">Constantin Stere</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Mihai_Eminescu" title="Mihai Eminescu">Mihai Eminescu</a>, a late <a href="/wiki/Romanticism" title="Romanticism">Romantic</a> poet, and <a href="/wiki/Ion_Creang%C4%83" title="Ion Creangă">Ion Creangă</a>, a writer, are the most influential <a href="/wiki/Romanian_language" title="Romanian language">Romanian language</a> artists, considered national writers both in Romania and Moldova.<sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cuisine">Cuisine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_cuisine" title="Moldovan cuisine">Moldovan cuisine</a></div>
<p>Moldova's fertile soil (<i><a href="/wiki/Chernozem" title="Chernozem">chernozem</a></i>) produces plentiful <a href="/wiki/Grapes" class="mw-redirect" title="Grapes">grapes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fruits" class="mw-redirect" title="Fruits">fruits</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vegetables" class="mw-redirect" title="Vegetables">vegetables</a>, <a href="/wiki/Food_grain" class="mw-redirect" title="Food grain">grains</a>, <a href="/wiki/Meat" title="Meat">meat</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Milk" title="Milk">milk</a> products, all of which have found their uses in the national cuisine. The fertile black soil combined with the use of traditional agricultural methods permits the growth of a wide range of foods in Moldova. Moldovan cuisine is similar to neighbouring <a href="/wiki/Romanian_cuisine" title="Romanian cuisine">Romania</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ukraine" title="Ukraine">Ukraine</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Poland" title="Poland">Poland</a>, and the regions share many traditional dishes in common, often with regional variations. Moldovan cuisine has historically been particularly influenced by elements of <a href="/wiki/Russian_cuisine" title="Russian cuisine">Russian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Turkish_cuisine" title="Turkish cuisine">Turkish</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ukrainian_cuisine" title="Ukrainian cuisine">Ukrainian cuisine</a>. Main dishes often include <a href="/wiki/Beef" title="Beef">beef</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pork" title="Pork">pork</a>, <a href="/wiki/Potatoes" class="mw-redirect" title="Potatoes">potatoes</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cabbage" title="Cabbage">cabbage</a>, and a variety of <a href="/wiki/Cereals" class="mw-redirect" title="Cereals">cereals</a>. Popular alcoholic beverages are <i><a href="/wiki/Moldovan_wine#Divin" title="Moldovan wine">divin</a></i> (Moldovan <a href="/wiki/Brandy" title="Brandy">brandy</a>), <a href="/wiki/Beer" title="Beer">beer</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_wine" title="Moldovan wine">wine</a>—of which the country is known for making high-quality offerings.<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:M%C4%83m%C4%83lig%C4%832020-02-12.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Mămăligă" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/M%C4%83m%C4%83lig%C4%832020-02-12.jpg/300px-M%C4%83m%C4%83lig%C4%832020-02-12.jpg" decoding="async" width="300" height="195" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/M%C4%83m%C4%83lig%C4%832020-02-12.jpg/450px-M%C4%83m%C4%83lig%C4%832020-02-12.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/M%C4%83m%C4%83lig%C4%832020-02-12.jpg/600px-M%C4%83m%C4%83lig%C4%832020-02-12.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1079" data-file-height="701" /></a><figcaption>Mămăligă</figcaption></figure>
<p>There are several traditional Moldovan dishes. <a href="/wiki/Pl%C4%83cint%C4%83" title="Plăcintă">Plăcinte</a> are stuffed and deep-fried pastries with fillings such as soft cheese (often <a href="/wiki/Urd%C4%83" title="Urdă">Urdă</a>), cabbage, potatoes, apples, sour cherries and others, either sweet or savoury.<sup id="cite_ref-339" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-339">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Sarma_(food)" title="Sarma (food)">Sarmale</a> is a typical Moldovan dish usually consisting of cabbage leaves stuffed with rice, peppers, carrots, meat, and baked in oil. Regional variations can also be found in other former parts of the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman Empire</a>. <a href="/wiki/M%C4%83m%C4%83lig%C4%83" title="Mămăligă">Mămăligă</a> is another staple, a kind of <a href="/wiki/Porridge" title="Porridge">porridge</a> made from yellow maize flour, and is popular in other countries but often named <a href="/wiki/Polenta" title="Polenta">polenta</a>, often served with <a href="/wiki/Sheep_milk_cheese" title="Sheep milk cheese">sheep's cheese</a> and <a href="/wiki/Sour_cream" title="Sour cream">sour cream</a>. Plachyndy is a kind of flatbread often made with <a href="/wiki/Kefir" title="Kefir">kefir</a> or <a href="/wiki/Buttermilk" title="Buttermilk">buttermilk</a>, wrapped around herbs and pan-fried in oil.<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup> Zeamă is a thin chicken soup, typically consists of homemade chicken broth that's prepared with a smaller whole chicken, water, thin homemade egg noodles (tăiței de casă), and a variety of finely chopped vegetables and herbs.<sup id="cite_ref-341" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-341">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Bryndza" title="Bryndza">Brynza</a> is a <a href="/wiki/Soft_cheese" class="mw-redirect" title="Soft cheese">soft</a> <a href="/wiki/Sheep_milk_cheese" title="Sheep milk cheese">sheep</a>/<a href="/wiki/Goat_cheese" title="Goat cheese">goat cheese</a> with a crumbly texture and tangy taste, mostly produced and popular in <a href="/wiki/Slovakia" title="Slovakia">Slovakia</a>, Romania, and Moldova, and often used in salads, pies, and dumplings.<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Borscht" title="Borscht">Borscht</a>, a sour <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Europe" title="Eastern Europe">Eastern European</a> soup made from beetroots, meat stock and vegetables, is also popular and commonly served in Moldova. As with other parts of the region, <a href="/wiki/Pierogi" title="Pierogi">pierogi</a> (called 'Chiroște' in Moldovan) are another traditional staple and are often stuffed with a soft cheese in Moldova. The dough is made with <a href="/wiki/Wheat_flour" title="Wheat flour">wheat flour</a> and is boiled in salted water, pan-fried in oil or baked in the oven.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Medovik" title="Medovik">Medovik</a>, a cake of Russian origin (and called Tort Smetanik in Moldova) is a popular layered cake with <a href="/wiki/Honey" title="Honey">honey</a> and <a href="/wiki/Smetana_(dairy_product)" title="Smetana (dairy product)">smetana</a> (sour cream) or <a href="/wiki/Condensed_milk" title="Condensed milk">condensed milk</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-345" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-345">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Total recorded adult alcohol consumption is approximately evenly split between spirits, beer and wine. Notably, Moldova has among the highest alcohol consumption per capita in world, at 15.2 litres (4.0&#160;US&#160;gal) of pure alcohol imbibed in 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup> This has fallen somewhat in recent years, but it remains a serious ongoing health concern.<sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Holidays">Holidays</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Public_holidays_in_Moldova" title="Public holidays in Moldova">Public holidays in Moldova</a></div>
<p>Most retail businesses close on <a href="/wiki/New_Year%27s_Day" title="New Year&#39;s Day">New Year's Day</a> and <a href="/wiki/Independence_Day_of_the_Republic_of_Moldova" title="Independence Day of the Republic of Moldova">Independence Day</a>, but remain open on all other holidays. <a href="/wiki/Christmas" title="Christmas">Christmas</a> is celebrated either on 7 January, the traditional date in <a href="/wiki/Old_Calendarists" title="Old Calendarists">Old Calendarists</a> <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church" title="Eastern Orthodox Church">Eastern Orthodox Churches</a>, or on 25 December, with both dates being recognized as public holidays.<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 1 March features <i><a href="/wiki/M%C4%83r%C8%9Bi%C8%99or" title="Mărțișor">mărțișor</a></i> gifting, which is a tradition that females are gifted with a type of talisman that is given for good luck.<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Music">Music</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Music_of_Moldova" title="Music of Moldova">Music of Moldova</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Moldova_at_ESC_2011.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Moldova_at_ESC_2011.jpg/220px-Moldova_at_ESC_2011.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Moldova_at_ESC_2011.jpg/330px-Moldova_at_ESC_2011.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Moldova_at_ESC_2011.jpg/440px-Moldova_at_ESC_2011.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1065" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Zdob_%C8%99i_Zdub" title="Zdob și Zdub">Zdob și Zdub</a> performing at the <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2011" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2011">2011 Eurovision Song Contest</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Among Moldova's most prominent composers are <a href="/wiki/Gavriil_Musicescu" title="Gavriil Musicescu">Gavriil Musicescu</a>, <a href="/wiki/%C8%98tefan_Neaga" title="Ștefan Neaga">Ștefan Neaga</a> and <a href="/wiki/Eugen_Doga" title="Eugen Doga">Eugen Doga</a>.
</p><p>In the field of pop music, Moldova has produced the band <a href="/wiki/O-Zone" title="O-Zone">O-Zone</a>, who came to prominence in 2003, with their hit song "<a href="/wiki/Dragostea_Din_Tei" title="Dragostea Din Tei">Dragostea Din Tei</a>", which topped multiple notable single charts. Moldova has been participating in the <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest" title="Eurovision Song Contest">Eurovision Song Contest</a> since 2005. Another popular band from Moldova is <a href="/wiki/Zdob_%C8%99i_Zdub" title="Zdob și Zdub">Zdob și Zdub</a> that represented the country in the <a href="/wiki/2005_Eurovision_Song_Contest" class="mw-redirect" title="2005 Eurovision Song Contest">2005 Eurovision Song Contest</a>, finishing sixth, also in 2021, with a similar result.
</p><p>In May 2007, <a href="/wiki/Natalia_Barbu" title="Natalia Barbu">Natalia Barbu</a> represented Moldova in Helsinki at the <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2007" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2007">Eurovision Song Contest 2007</a> with her entry "<a href="/wiki/Fight_(song)" class="mw-redirect" title="Fight (song)">Fight</a>". Natalia squeezed into the final by a very small margin. She took tenth place with 109 points.
Then <a href="/wiki/Zdob_%C8%99i_Zdub" title="Zdob și Zdub">Zdob și Zdub</a> again represented Moldova in the <a href="/wiki/2011_Eurovision_Song_Contest" class="mw-redirect" title="2011 Eurovision Song Contest">2011 Eurovision Song Contest</a> finishing 12th.
</p><p>The band <a href="/wiki/SunStroke_Project" title="SunStroke Project">SunStroke Project</a> with <a href="/wiki/Olia_Tira" title="Olia Tira">Olia Tira</a> represented the country in the <a href="/wiki/2010_Eurovision_Song_Contest" class="mw-redirect" title="2010 Eurovision Song Contest">2010 Eurovision Song Contest</a> with their hit song "<a href="/wiki/Run_Away_(SunStroke_Project_and_Olia_Tira_song)" title="Run Away (SunStroke Project and Olia Tira song)">Run Away</a>". Their performance gained international notoriety as an <a href="/wiki/Internet_meme" title="Internet meme">internet meme</a> due to the pelvic thrusting and dancing of Sergey Stepanov, the band saxophonist. He has been dubbed "<a href="/wiki/Epic_Sax_Guy" class="mw-redirect" title="Epic Sax Guy">Epic Sax Guy</a>". SunStroke Project featured again in the 2017 Eurovision entry "Hey Mama" which got third place.<sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2015 a new musical project by the name of <a href="/wiki/Carla%27s_Dreams" title="Carla&#39;s Dreams">Carla's Dreams</a> has risen in popularity around Moldova. <a href="/wiki/Carla%27s_Dreams" title="Carla&#39;s Dreams">Carla's Dreams</a> reached the top charts in multiple countries in Europe with the release of their song "Sub Pielea Mea" in 2016. The song received a lot of airplay and reached number one place on the charts in Moldova as well as Russia. The group is still active and released their latest album in 2017. The theme of the musical group is "Anonymous" as they perform with painted faces, hoodies and sunglasses. The identity of the group members is still unknown.
</p><p>Among most prominent classical musicians in Moldova are <a href="/wiki/Maria_Bie%C8%99u" title="Maria Bieșu">Maria Bieșu</a>, one of the leading world's sopranos and the winner of the Japan International Competition; pianist <a href="/wiki/Mark_Zeltser" title="Mark Zeltser">Mark Zeltser</a>, winner of the USSR National Competition, <a href="/wiki/Long-Thibaud-Crespin_Competition" title="Long-Thibaud-Crespin Competition">Long-Thibaud-Crespin Competition</a> in Paris and Busoni Competition in Bolzano, Italy.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Media">Media</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Media_of_Moldova" class="mw-redirect" title="Media of Moldova">Media of Moldova</a>, <a href="/wiki/Television_in_Moldova" title="Television in Moldova">Television in Moldova</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Moldova" title="Cinema of Moldova">Cinema of Moldova</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_newspapers_in_Moldova" title="List of newspapers in Moldova">List of newspapers in Moldova</a></div>
<p>The right to <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_speech" title="Freedom of speech">freedom of speech</a> and <a href="/wiki/Right_to_information" class="mw-redirect" title="Right to information">right to information</a> are guaranteed by the <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_constitution" class="mw-redirect" title="Moldovan constitution">Moldovan constitution</a>. <a href="/wiki/Reporters_Without_Borders" title="Reporters Without Borders">Reporters Without Borders</a> improved Moldova's <a href="/wiki/World_Press_Freedom_Index" title="World Press Freedom Index">Press Freedom Index</a> ranking to 28th in 2023 from 89th in 2020, partly due to government legal reforms which made it easier for journalists to access official information.<sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup> However, they cautioned that "Moldova's media are diverse but extremely polarised, like the country itself, which is marked by political instability and excessive influence by oligarchs." Moldova's media are divided into pro-Russian and pro-Western camps and on party political lines.<sup id="cite_ref-:07_353-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:07-353">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup> Oligarchs and political leaders strongly influence their editorial stances.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Television" title="Television">Television</a> remains the most popular and trusted medium, while online <a href="/wiki/Social_media" title="Social media">social media</a> is exerting increasing influence. Most private <a href="/wiki/FM_broadcasting" title="FM broadcasting">FM radio networks</a> rebroadcast output from Russian and Romanian stations.<sup id="cite_ref-:07_353-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:07-353">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup> The first <a href="/wiki/Public_broadcasting" title="Public broadcasting">publicly-funded national radio broadcaster</a>, <a href="/wiki/Radio_Moldova" title="Radio Moldova">Radio Moldova</a>, has been broadcasting since 1939 from the capital city, Chişinău. <a href="/wiki/Radio_Free_Europe/Radio_Liberty" title="Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty">Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty</a> is also widely available. Moldova's state-owned national radio-TV broadcaster is <a href="/wiki/Teleradio-Moldova" title="Teleradio-Moldova">Teleradio-Moldova</a> (TRM), which broadcasts the TV channel <a href="/wiki/Moldova_1" title="Moldova 1">Moldova 1</a>.
</p><p>There were 3 million internet users by July 2022, approximately 76% of the population, and digital infrastructure is well-developed, with 98% <a href="/wiki/4G" title="4G">4G</a> coverage of territory. There are a number of daily and weekly newspapers published in Moldova, among the most popular being <i><a href="/wiki/Timpul_de_diminea%C8%9B%C4%83" title="Timpul de dimineață">Timpul de dimineață</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Moldova_Suveran%C4%83" title="Moldova Suverană">Moldova Suverană</a>,</i> but print media has an overall small audience in Moldova<i>.</i> <a href="/wiki/Independent_media" title="Independent media">Independent media</a> are struggling to ensure financial sustainability in the face of diminishing advertisement revenues due to inflation, economic stagnation and uncertainty caused by Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
</p><p>In 2022, the government removed the broadcasting licenses from six <a href="/wiki/Television_station" title="Television station">television stations</a> for broadcasting <a href="/wiki/Propaganda_in_Russia" title="Propaganda in Russia">pro-Russian propaganda</a> and disinformation about <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russia's invasion of Ukraine</a> in violation of the country's Audiovisual Services Code.<sup id="cite_ref-354" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-354">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> The government stated that this was done in order to "prevent the risk of disinformation or attempts to manipulate public opinion".<sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup> All six were either owned or affiliated with <a href="/wiki/Ilan_Shor" title="Ilan Shor">Ilan Șhor</a>, a fugitive pro-Russian politician and businessman who fled to <a href="/wiki/Israel" title="Israel">Israel</a> in 2019 after being convicted of fraud and money-laundering and sentenced to 15 years in prison <i>in absentia</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Moldova" title="Cinema of Moldova">cinema of Moldova</a> developed in the 1960s during the Soviet period, nurturing a small but lively film industry.<sup id="cite_ref-:12_357-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:12-357">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup> Following the collapse of the Soviet Union and Moldova's independence, the country's economic stagnation and poverty has hampered the Moldovan film industry.<sup id="cite_ref-:12_357-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:12-357">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-358" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-358">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> Nevertheless, some films have seen some international success. Perhaps best-known are <i><a href="/wiki/L%C4%83utarii" title="Lăutarii">Lăutarii</a></i> (1972), written and directed by Moldovan film-maker <a href="/wiki/Emil_Loteanu" title="Emil Loteanu">Emil Loteanu</a>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Wedding_in_Bessarabia" title="Wedding in Bessarabia">Wedding in Bessarabia</a></i> (2009), which was co-produced by Romania, Moldova, and Luxembourg. In recent years Moldovan cinema has gained greater international attention. <i>Carbon</i> (2022), directed by Ion Borş, received positive acclaim by magazines such as Variety.<sup id="cite_ref-359" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-359">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup> It was the winner of the <a href="/wiki/Transilvania_International_Film_Festival" title="Transilvania International Film Festival">Transilvania International Film Festival</a>'s Audience Award.<sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup> For the 37th edition of the <a href="/wiki/Fribourg_International_Film_Festival" title="Fribourg International Film Festival">Fribourg International Film Festival</a>, Moldova was featured in its 'New Territory' section, which celebrates little-known film-making cultures.<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup> In July 2022, the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Development_Programme" title="United Nations Development Programme">United Nations Development Programme</a> announced that it would be using state-of-the-art equipment to transfer more than 1,600 films from the <a href="/wiki/Moldova-Film" title="Moldova-Film">Moldova-Film</a> archive for posterity and <a href="/wiki/Cultural_preservation" class="mw-redirect" title="Cultural preservation">cultural preservation</a>. The <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</a> assisted by equipping in 2021 a <a href="/wiki/Digitization" title="Digitization">digitization</a> laboratory to restore and preserve its archive feature and documentary films, representing an important part of Moldova's historical, cultural, and artistic heritage, and many of the films were broadcast on national TV with Romanian subtitles.<sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Sports">Sports</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Sport_in_Moldova" title="Sport in Moldova">Sport in Moldova</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:AUT_vs._MDA_2015-09-05_(006).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/AUT_vs._MDA_2015-09-05_%28006%29.jpg/220px-AUT_vs._MDA_2015-09-05_%28006%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/AUT_vs._MDA_2015-09-05_%28006%29.jpg/330px-AUT_vs._MDA_2015-09-05_%28006%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/AUT_vs._MDA_2015-09-05_%28006%29.jpg/440px-AUT_vs._MDA_2015-09-05_%28006%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3000" data-file-height="2000" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Moldova_national_football_team" title="Moldova national football team">Moldova national football team</a> in 2015</figcaption></figure><p><a href="/wiki/Association_football" title="Association football">Association football</a> is the most popular team sport in Moldova. The governing body is the <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_Football_Federation" title="Moldovan Football Federation">Moldovan Football Federation</a>, which belongs to <a href="/wiki/UEFA" title="UEFA">UEFA</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Moldova_national_football_team" title="Moldova national football team">Moldova national football team</a> played its first match in 1994, but never qualified to the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship" title="UEFA European Championship">UEFA European Championship</a>. The most successful football club is <a href="/wiki/FC_Sheriff_Tiraspol" title="FC Sheriff Tiraspol">Sheriff Tiraspol</a>, the first and only Moldovan club to qualify for the group stage of the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League" title="UEFA Champions League">Champions League</a> and the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League" title="UEFA Europa League">Europa League</a>. Other winners of the <a href="/wiki/Moldovan_National_Division" class="mw-redirect" title="Moldovan National Division">Moldovan National Division</a> include <a href="/wiki/FC_Zimbru_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="FC Zimbru Chișinău">Zimbru Chișinău</a>, <a href="/wiki/FC_Dacia_Chi%C8%99in%C4%83u" title="FC Dacia Chișinău">Dacia Chișinău</a>, <a href="/wiki/FC_Tiraspol" title="FC Tiraspol">FC Tiraspol</a> and <a href="/wiki/FC_Milsami_Orhei" title="FC Milsami Orhei">Milsami Orhei</a>.
</p><p><i><a href="/wiki/Tr%C3%AEnt%C4%83" class="mw-redirect" title="Trîntă">Trîntă</a></i> (a form of <a href="/wiki/Wrestling" title="Wrestling">wrestling</a>) is the national sport in Moldova. <a href="/wiki/Rugby_union" title="Rugby union">Rugby union</a> is popular as well. More than 10,000 supporters turn out for home internationals. Since 2004, playing numbers at all levels have more than doubled to 3,200. Despite the hardships and deprivations the national team are ranked 34th in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-364" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-364">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup> The most prestigious <a href="/wiki/Cycling_race" class="mw-redirect" title="Cycling race">cycling race</a> is the <a href="/wiki/Moldova_President%27s_Cup" title="Moldova President&#39;s Cup">Moldova President's Cup</a>, which was first run in 2004. In chess, the Republic of Moldova has several international masters, among which can be mentioned <a href="/wiki/Viorel_Iord%C4%83chescu" title="Viorel Iordăchescu">Viorel Iordăchescu</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dmitry_Svetushkin" title="Dmitry Svetushkin">Dmitry Svetushkin</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Victor_Bologan" title="Victor Bologan">Viorel Bologan</a>.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Radu_Albot" title="Radu Albot">Radu Albot</a> is one of the most successful Moldovan tennis players, with <a href="/wiki/Association_of_Tennis_Professionals" title="Association of Tennis Professionals">ATP</a> singles (<a href="/wiki/2019_Delray_Beach_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles" title="2019 Delray Beach Open – Singles">2019 Delray Beach Open</a>) and doubles (<a href="/wiki/2015_Istanbul_Open_%E2%80%93_Doubles" title="2015 Istanbul Open – Doubles">2015 Istanbul Open</a>) titles.
</p><p>Athletes from Moldova have won European medals in <a href="/wiki/Track_and_field" title="Track and field">athletics</a>, <a href="/wiki/Biathlon" title="Biathlon">biathlon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Association_football" title="Association football">football</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Gymnastics" title="Gymnastics">gymnastics</a>; world medals in <a href="/wiki/Archery" title="Archery">archery</a>, <a href="/wiki/Judo" title="Judo">judo</a>, <a href="/wiki/Swimming_(sport)" title="Swimming (sport)">swimming</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Taekwondo" title="Taekwondo">taekwondo</a>; as well as <a href="/wiki/Olympic_Games" title="Olympic Games">Olympic</a> medals in <a href="/wiki/Boxing" title="Boxing">boxing</a>, <a href="/wiki/Canoeing" title="Canoeing">canoeing</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shooting_sports" title="Shooting sports">shooting</a>, <a href="/wiki/Olympic_weightlifting" title="Olympic weightlifting">weightlifting</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Amateur_wrestling" title="Amateur wrestling">wrestling</a>. Moldova made its Olympic debut at the <a href="/wiki/1994_Winter_Olympics" title="1994 Winter Olympics">1994 Winter Olympics</a> in Lillehammer. Olympic medalists include <a href="/wiki/Sergei_Mureiko" title="Sergei Mureiko">Sergei Mureiko</a>, <a href="/wiki/Oleg_Moldovan" title="Oleg Moldovan">Oleg Moldovan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vitalie_Gru%C8%99ac" title="Vitalie Grușac">Vitalie Grușac</a>, <a href="/wiki/Veaceslav_Gojan" title="Veaceslav Gojan">Veaceslav Gojan</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Serghei_Tarnovschi" title="Serghei Tarnovschi">Serghei Tarnovschi</a>. <a href="/wiki/Nicolae_Juravschi" title="Nicolae Juravschi">Nicolae Juravschi</a> represented the Soviet Union at the <a href="/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics" title="1988 Summer Olympics">1988 Seoul Games</a>, winning two medals.
</p>
